bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 起強圉協洽，盡昭陽赤奮若，凡七年。

translations.literal: From Qianggu Xiehe through Zhaoyang Chifenruo; seven years in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Qianggu Xiehe through Zhaoyang Chifenruo—seven years in all.

sentences.zh: 1春，二月，詔減口賦錢什三。

translations.literal: 1. In spring, the second month, an edict reduced the poll tax by three-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, the second month, an edict cut the poll tax by thirty percent.

sentences.zh: ----2夏，四月，癸未，帝崩於未央宮；

translations.literal: ----2 In summer, the fourth month, on guiwei, the emperor died at Weiyang Palace;
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In summer, the fourth month, on guiwei, the emperor died at Weiyang Palace;

sentences.zh: 無嗣。

translations.literal: he left no heir.
translations.idiomatic: he left no heir.

sentences.zh: 時武帝子獨有廣陵王胥，大將軍光與群臣議所立，咸持廣陵王。

translations.literal: At that time among Emperor Wu's sons only the Prince of Guangling, Xu, remained; Grand General Guang and the ministers debated whom to establish, and all favored the Prince of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Wu's only surviving son was Prince Xu of Guangling; Grand General Guang and the ministers debated whom to enthrone, and all favored the Prince of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 王本以行失道，先帝所不用；

translations.literal: The prince had long since lost the Way in his conduct and had been passed over by the former emperor;
translations.idiomatic: The prince had long since lost the Way in his conduct and had been passed over by the former emperor;

sentences.zh: 光內不自安。

translations.literal: Guang inwardly was ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was inwardly ill at ease.

sentences.zh: 朗有上書言：「周太王廢太伯立王季，文王捨伯邑考立武王，唯在所宜，雖廢長立少可也。

translations.literal: A gentleman of the Lang submitted a memorial, saying: "King Tai of Zhou set aside Taibo and established Wang Ji; King Wen set aside Boyi Kao and established King Wu—only fitness matters; though one abolishes the elder to establish the younger, it may be done.
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman of the Lang submitted a memorial: "King Tai of Zhou set aside Taibo and established Wang Ji; King Wen set aside Boyi Kao and established King Wu—only fitness matters; abolishing the elder to establish the younger can be right.

sentences.zh: 廣陵王不可以承宗廟。

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangling cannot undertake the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guangling cannot undertake the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 」言合光意。

translations.literal: " The words accorded with Guang's intent.
translations.idiomatic: " The words accorded with Guang's intent.

sentences.zh: 光以其書示丞相敞等，擢郎為九江太守。

translations.literal: Guang showed the memorial to Chancellor Chang and the others and promoted the gentleman to Governor of Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Guang showed the memorial to Chancellor Chang and the others and promoted the gentleman to Governor of Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 即日承皇后詔，遣行大鴻臚事少府樂成、宗正德、光祿大夫吉、中郎將利漢，迎昌邑王賀，乘七乘傳詣長安邸。

translations.literal: That same day, acting on the empress dowager's edict, he sent the Acting Grand Herald, Director of the Palace Treasury Yuecheng, Director of the Imperial Clan De, Palace Grandee Ji, and Palace Cadet General Li Han to welcome the Prince of Changyi, He, who traveled by seven-relay post carriage to the Chang'an residence.
translations.idiomatic: That same day, acting on the empress dowager's edict, he sent Acting Grand Herald Yuecheng, Director of the Imperial Clan De, Palace Grandee Ji, and Palace Cadet General Li Han to welcome Prince He of Changyi, who traveled by seven-relay post carriage to the Chang'an residence.

sentences.zh: 光又白皇后，徒右將軍安世為車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Guang also reported to the empress dowager and transferred Right General Anshi to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Guang also reported to the empress dowager and transferred Right General Anshi to General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 賀，昌邑哀王之子也，在國素狂縱，動作無節。

translations.literal: He was son of King Ai of Changyi and in his domain had always been wild and unrestrained, his conduct without measure.
translations.idiomatic: He was the son of King Ai of Changyi and in his domain had always been wild and unrestrained, his conduct without measure.

sentences.zh: 武帝之喪，賀遊獵不止。

translations.literal: During Emperor Wu's mourning, He did not cease hunting and roaming.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Wu's mourning, He never stopped hunting and roaming.

sentences.zh: 嘗遊方與，不半日馳二百里。

translations.literal: Once while touring Fangyu he galloped two hundred li in less than half a day.
translations.idiomatic: Once while touring Fangyu he galloped two hundred li in less than half a day.

sentences.zh: 中尉琅邪王吉上疏諫曰：「大王不好書術而樂逸游，馮式撙銜，馳騁不止，口倦虖叱吒，手苦於棰轡，身勞虖車輿，朝則冒霧露，晝則被塵埃，夏則為大暑之所暴炙，冬則為風寒之所匽薄，數以耎脆之玉體犯勤勞之煩毒，非所以全壽命之宗也，又非所以進仁義之隆也。

translations.literal: Commandant Wang Ji of Langye submitted a memorial of admonition, saying: "Your Highness does not love books and arts but delights in roaming at ease, gripping the reins in driving posture and galloping without cease—your mouth weary from shouting and roaring, your hands tormented by whip and bridle, your body worn by carriage and chariot; in the morning you meet mist and dew, by day you are clothed in dust; in summer you are scorched by great heat, in winter you are pelted by wind and cold. Repeatedly you set this tender, fragile jade body against toilsome harm—not the way to preserve the root of long life, nor the way to advance the height of benevolence and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Wang Ji of Langye submitted a memorial of admonition: "Your Highness does not love books and the arts but delights in roaming at ease—gripping the reins, galloping without cease. Your mouth grows weary from shouting; your hands ache from whip and bridle; your body is worn by carriage and chariot. In the morning you meet mist and dew; by day you are clothed in dust; in summer you are scorched by great heat; in winter you are pelted by wind and cold. Again and again you set this tender, fragile body against toilsome harm—not the way to preserve long life, nor to advance benevolence and righteousness."

sentences.zh: 夫廣廈之下，細旃之上，明師居前，勤誦在後，上論唐、虞之際，下及殷、周之盛，考仁聖之風，習治國之道，訢訢焉發憤忘食，日新厥德，其樂豈銜橛之間哉！

translations.literal: Under a broad hall, upon fine felt, with an enlightened teacher before you and diligent recitation behind, discoursing above on the age of Tang and Yu and reaching below to the splendor of Yin and Zhou, examining the winds of benevolence and sagehood and practicing the Way of governing the state—eagerly forgetting food in ardent study, renewing your virtue day by day—would its joy be merely between bit and curb!
translations.idiomatic: Under a broad hall, upon fine felt, with an enlightened teacher before you and diligent recitation behind—discoursing on the age of Tang and Yu, reaching down to the splendor of Yin and Zhou, examining the winds of benevolence and sagehood, practicing the Way of governing the state—eagerly forgetting food in ardent study, renewing your virtue day by day—would its joy be merely between bit and curb!"

sentences.zh: 休則俛仰屈伸以利形，進退步趨以實下，吸新吐故以練臧，專意積精以適神，於以養生，豈不長哉！

translations.literal: In rest, bend and stretch to benefit the form; advance and retreat, step and pace to strengthen the lower body; draw in the new and expel the old to train the viscera; focus the mind and gather essence to suit the spirit—in this way to nourish life, is it not long-lasting!
translations.idiomatic: In rest, bend and stretch to benefit the form; advance and retreat, step and pace to strengthen the lower body; draw in the new and expel the old to train the viscera; focus the mind and gather essence to suit the spirit—in this way to nourish life, is it not lasting!"

sentences.zh: 大王誠留意如此，則心有堯、舜之志，體有喬、松之壽，美聲廣譽，登而上聞，則福祿其臻而社稷安矣。

translations.literal: If Your Highness truly heed this, then your heart will hold the intent of Yao and Shun, your body the longevity of Qiao and Song, fine renown and broad praise mounting to reach those above, and fortune and emolument will arrive while the altars of soil and grain are secure.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness truly heed this, your heart will hold the intent of Yao and Shun, your body the longevity of Qiao and Song; fine renown will mount to those above, fortune will arrive, and the altars of soil and grain will be secure."

sentences.zh: 皇帝仁聖，至今思慕未怠，於宮館、囿池、戈獵之樂未有所幸，大王宜夙夜念此以承聖意。

translations.literal: The emperor was benevolent and sage; to this day his mourning has not slackened. He never indulged in the pleasures of palaces, parks, ponds, arms, or hunting. Your Highness ought day and night to keep this in mind to carry out his intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was benevolent and sage; to this day his mourning has not slackened. He never indulged in palaces, parks, ponds, arms, or hunting. Your Highness ought day and night to keep this in mind and carry out his intent."

sentences.zh: 諸侯骨肉，莫親大王，大王於屬則子也，於位則臣也，一身而二任之責加焉。

translations.literal: Among the feudal lords in flesh and bone, none is closer than Your Highness. In kinship you are a son; in station you are a subject—upon one person the double burden of both offices is laid.
translations.idiomatic: Among the feudal lords in flesh and bone, none is closer than Your Highness. In kinship you are a son; in station you are a subject—upon one person the double burden of both offices is laid."

sentences.zh: 恩愛行義，孅介有不具者，於以上聞，非饗國之福也。

translations.literal: If in affection, conduct, or the slightest propriety anything is lacking and it reaches those above, it is not the blessing of a state that enjoys offerings.
translations.idiomatic: If in affection, conduct, or the slightest propriety anything is lacking and it reaches those above, it is not the blessing of a state that enjoys offerings."

sentences.zh: 」王乃下令曰：「寡人造行不能無惰，中尉其忠，數輔吾過。

translations.literal: " The prince thereupon issued an order: "My conduct cannot be without sloth; the Commandant is loyal and repeatedly assists my faults.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince issued an order: "My conduct cannot be without sloth; the Commandant is loyal and repeatedly corrects my faults."

sentences.zh: 」使謁者千秋賜中尉牛肉五百斤，酒五石，脯五束。

translations.literal: " He sent the Usher Qianqiu to bestow on the Commandant five hundred jin of beef, five piculs of wine, and five bundles of dried meat.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent Usher Qianqiu to bestow on the Commandant five hundred jin of beef, five piculs of wine, and five bundles of dried meat.

sentences.zh: 其後復放縱自若。

translations.literal: Afterward he again gave himself to wild license as before.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he again gave himself to wild license as before.

sentences.zh: 郎中令山陽龔遂，忠厚剛毅，有大節，內諫爭於王，外責傅相，引經義，陳禍福，至於涕泣，蹇蹇亡已，面刺王過。

translations.literal: Director of the Gentlemen Gong Sui of Shanyang was loyal, thick, firm, and resolute, with great integrity; inwardly he remonstrated with the prince, outwardly he held the tutor and chancellor to account, citing canonical principles and laying out fortune and calamity until he wept, steadfast and unceasing, confronting the prince's faults to his face.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Gentlemen Gong Sui of Shanyang was loyal, steadfast, and resolute, with great integrity; inwardly he remonstrated with the prince, outwardly he held the tutor and chancellor to account, citing canonical principles and laying out fortune and calamity until he wept—steadfast and unceasing, confronting the prince's faults to his face.

sentences.zh: 王至掩耳起走，曰：「郎中令善愧人！

translations.literal: The prince would cover his ears, rise, and flee, saying: "The Director of the Gentlemen is skilled at shaming people!
translations.idiomatic: The prince would cover his ears, rise, and flee, saying, "The Director of the Gentlemen is skilled at shaming people!"

sentences.zh: 」王嘗久與騶奴、宰人遊戲飲食，賞賜無度，遂入見王，涕泣膝行，左右侍御皆出涕。

translations.literal: " Once the prince spent long days gaming, eating, and drinking with grooms, slaves, and cooks, bestowing rewards without measure. Sui entered to see the prince, weeping and advancing on his knees; attendants left and right all shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: " Once the prince spent long days gaming, eating, and drinking with grooms, slaves, and cooks, bestowing rewards without measure. Sui entered to see the prince, weeping and advancing on his knees; attendants left and right all shed tears.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「郎中令何為哭？

translations.literal: The prince said: "Director of the Gentlemen, why do you weep?
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "Director of the Gentlemen, why do you weep?"

sentences.zh: 」遂曰：「臣痛社稷危也！

translations.literal: " Sui said: "Your servant grieves that the altars of soil and grain are in peril!
translations.idiomatic: " Sui said, "Your servant grieves that the altars of soil and grain are in peril!"

sentences.zh: 願賜清閒，竭愚！

translations.literal: I beg leave for a quiet audience to exhaust my foolishness!
translations.idiomatic: I beg a quiet audience to exhaust my foolish counsel!"

sentences.zh: 」王辟左右。

translations.literal: " The prince dismissed those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince dismissed those at his side.

sentences.zh: 遂曰：「大王知膠西王所以為無道亡乎？

translations.literal: Sui said: "Does Your Highness know why the Prince of Jiaoxi became lawless and perished?
translations.idiomatic: Sui said, "Does Your Highness know why the Prince of Jiaoxi became lawless and perished?"

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「不知也。

translations.literal: " The prince said: "I do not know.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince said, "I do not know."

sentences.zh: 」曰：「臣聞膠西王有諛臣侯得，王所為擬於桀、紂也，得以為堯、舜也。

translations.literal: " He said: "Your servant has heard that the Prince of Jiaoxi had a flatterer, Hou De; what the prince did resembled Jie and Zhou, yet De called it Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "Your servant has heard that the Prince of Jiaoxi had a flatterer, Hou De; what the prince did resembled Jie and Zhou, yet De called it Yao and Shun."

sentences.zh: 王說其諂諛，常與寢處，唯得所言，以至於是。

translations.literal: The prince delighted in his flattery, constantly shared bed and dwelling with him, and heeded only what De said—until it came to this.
translations.idiomatic: The prince delighted in his flattery, constantly shared bed and dwelling with him, and heeded only what De said—until it came to this."

sentences.zh: 今大王親近群小，漸漬邪惡所習，存亡之機，不可不慎也！

translations.literal: Now Your Highness draws near petty men, steeped in what evil habits instill—the hinge of survival and extinction cannot be treated lightly!
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Highness draws near petty men, steeped in what evil habits instill—the hinge of survival and extinction cannot be treated lightly!"

sentences.zh: 臣請選郎通經有行義者與王起成，坐則誦《詩》、《書》，立則習禮容，宜有益。

translations.literal: Your servant asks to select gentlemen of the Lang who know the classics and possess conduct and righteousness to rise and sit with Your Highness—when seated to recite the Odes and Documents, when standing to practice ritual deportment; it should be of benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant asks to select gentlemen of the Lang who know the classics and possess conduct and righteousness to rise and sit with Your Highness—when seated to recite the Odes and Documents, when standing to practice ritual deportment; it should help."

sentences.zh: 」王許之。

translations.literal: " The prince assented.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince assented.

sentences.zh: 遂乃選郎中張安等十人侍王。

translations.literal: Sui thereupon selected Palace Gentlemen Zhang An and nine others to attend the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Sui selected Palace Gentlemen Zhang An and nine others to attend the prince.

sentences.zh: 居數日，王皆逐去安等。

translations.literal: Within several days the prince drove out An and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Within several days the prince drove out An and the rest.

sentences.zh: 王嘗見大白犬，頸以下似人，冠方山冠而無尾，以問龔遂，遂曰：「此天戒，言在側者盡冠狗也，去之則存，不去則亡矣。

translations.literal: The prince once saw a great white dog, from the neck down like a man, wearing a fangshan cap but without a tail. He asked Gong Sui; Sui said: "This is a heaven-sent warning, saying those at your side are all capped dogs; remove them and you survive—fail to remove them and you perish.
translations.idiomatic: The prince once saw a great white dog, from the neck down like a man, wearing a fangshan cap but without a tail. He asked Gong Sui; Sui said, "This is a heaven-sent warning: those at your side are all capped dogs; remove them and you survive—fail to remove them and you perish."

sentences.zh: 」後又聞人聲曰：「熊！

translations.literal: " Later he again heard a human voice say: "Bear!
translations.idiomatic: " Later he again heard a human voice say, "Bear!"

sentences.zh: 」視而見大熊，左右莫見，以問遂，遂曰：「熊，山野之獸，而來入宮室，王獨見之，此天戒大王，恐宮室將空，危亡象也。

translations.literal: " He looked and saw a great bear; those left and right saw nothing. He asked Sui; Sui said: "The bear is a beast of mountain and wild, yet it came into the palace chambers and Your Highness alone saw it. This is heaven's warning to Your Highness: I fear the chambers will be emptied—the image of peril and extinction.
translations.idiomatic: " He looked and saw a great bear; those left and right saw nothing. He asked Sui; Sui said, "The bear is a beast of mountain and wild, yet it came into the palace chambers and Your Highness alone saw it. This is heaven's warning: I fear the chambers will be emptied—the image of peril and extinction."

sentences.zh: 」王仰天而歎曰：「不祥何為數來！

translations.literal: " The prince looked up to heaven and sighed: "Why do ill omens come again and again!
translations.idiomatic: " The prince looked up to heaven and sighed, "Why do ill omens come again and again!"

sentences.zh: 」遂叩頭曰：「臣不敢隱忠，數言危亡之戒；

translations.literal: " Sui knocked his head on the ground and said: "Your servant dares not conceal loyalty; I have repeatedly spoken warnings of peril and extinction;
translations.idiomatic: " Sui knocked his head on the ground and said, "Your servant dares not conceal loyalty; I have repeatedly spoken warnings of peril and extinction;"

sentences.zh: 大王不說。

translations.literal: Your Highness is not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness is not pleased."

sentences.zh: 夫國之存亡，豈在臣言哉！

translations.literal: Whether the state survives or perishes—how could it depend on your servant's words!
translations.idiomatic: Whether the state survives or perishes—how could it depend on my words!"

sentences.zh: 願王內自揆度。

translations.literal: I beg Your Highness inwardly to measure and reflect.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Highness inwardly to measure and reflect."

sentences.zh: 大王誦《詩》三百五篇，人事浹，王道備。

translations.literal: Your Highness recites the three hundred and five pieces of the Odes—human affairs are thorough, the kingly Way complete.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness recites the three hundred and five pieces of the Odes—human affairs are thorough, the kingly Way complete."

sentences.zh: 王之所行，中《詩》一篇何等也？

translations.literal: In what Your Highness does, which single piece of the Odes does it match?
translations.idiomatic: In what Your Highness does, which single piece of the Odes does it match?"

sentences.zh: 大王位於諸侯王，行污於庶人，以存難，以亡易，宜深察之！

translations.literal: Your Highness stands among feudal kings yet acts fouler than a commoner—to preserve is hard, to perish is easy; you ought to examine this deeply!
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness stands among feudal kings yet acts fouler than a commoner—to preserve is hard, to perish is easy; you ought to examine this deeply!"

sentences.zh: 」後又血污王坐席，王問遂；

translations.literal: " Later blood again stained the prince's seat; the prince asked Sui;
translations.idiomatic: " Later blood again stained the prince's seat; the prince asked Sui;

sentences.zh: 遂叫然號曰：「宮空不久，妖祥數至。

translations.literal: Sui cried out in a shout: "The chambers will soon be empty; prodigies and omens arrive in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Sui cried out: "The chambers will soon be empty; prodigies and omens arrive in succession."

sentences.zh: 血者，陰憂象也，宜畏慎自省！

translations.literal: Blood is the image of yin sorrow; you ought to fear, be cautious, and examine yourself!
translations.idiomatic: Blood is the image of yin sorrow; you ought to fear, be cautious, and examine yourself!"

sentences.zh: 」王終不改節。

translations.literal: " The prince in the end did not change his ways.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince in the end did not change his ways.

sentences.zh: 及徵書至，夜漏未盡一刻，以火發書。

translations.literal: When the summons arrived, before one quarter of the night watch had passed he opened the letter by firelight.
translations.idiomatic: When the summons arrived, before one quarter of the night watch had passed he opened the letter by firelight.

sentences.zh: 其日中，王發；

translations.literal: At midday the prince set out;
translations.idiomatic: At midday the prince set out;

sentences.zh: 晡時，至定陶，行百三十五里，侍從者馬死相望於道。

translations.literal: at the hour of shen he reached Dingtao, having traveled one hundred thirty-five li; among his attendants horses died one after another along the road.
translations.idiomatic: at the hour of shen he reached Dingtao, having traveled one hundred thirty-five li; among his attendants horses died one after another along the road.

sentences.zh: 王吉奏書戒王曰：「臣聞高宗諒闇，三年不言。

translations.literal: Wang Ji submitted a memorial warning the prince: "Your servant has heard that Gaozong observed deep mourning and for three years did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji submitted a memorial warning the prince: "Your servant has heard that Gaozong observed deep mourning and for three years did not speak."

sentences.zh: 今大王以喪事徵，宜日夜哭泣悲哀而已，慎毋有所發！

translations.literal: Now Your Highness is summoned for the mourning rites; you ought only to weep and grieve day and night—take care to initiate nothing!
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Highness is summoned for the mourning rites; you ought only to weep and grieve day and night—take care to initiate nothing!"

sentences.zh: 大將軍仁愛、勇智、忠信之德，天下莫不聞；

translations.literal: The Grand General's virtues of benevolence, love, courage, wisdom, loyalty, and trustworthiness—none under Heaven has not heard of them;
translations.idiomatic: The Grand General's virtues of benevolence, courage, wisdom, loyalty, and trustworthiness—none under Heaven has not heard of them;"

sentences.zh: 事孝武皇帝二十餘年，未嘗有過。

translations.literal: he served Emperor Xiao of Wu for more than twenty years and never once had a fault.
translations.idiomatic: he served Emperor Xiao of Wu for more than twenty years without a single fault."

sentences.zh: 先帝棄群臣，屬以天下，寄幼孤焉。

translations.literal: The former emperor left his ministers, entrusted him with all under Heaven, and placed the young orphan in his care.
translations.idiomatic: The former emperor left his ministers, entrusted him with all under Heaven, and placed the young orphan in his care."

sentences.zh: 大將軍抱持幼君襁褓之中，布政施教，海內晏然，雖周公、伊尹無以加也。

translations.literal: The Grand General held the young lord from swaddling clothes, spread government and taught the people, and within the seas all was tranquil—even the Duke of Zhou and Yi Yin could not surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand General held the young lord from swaddling clothes, spread government and taught the people, and within the seas all was tranquil—even the Duke of Zhou and Yi Yin could not surpass him."

sentences.zh: 今帝崩無嗣，大將軍惟思可以奉宗廟者，攀援而立大王，其仁厚豈有量哉！

translations.literal: Now the emperor has died without an heir; the Grand General has pondered only who can serve the ancestral temple, and drawing support has established Your Highness—how can his benevolence and depth be measured!
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor has died without an heir; the Grand General has pondered only who can serve the ancestral temple and, drawing support, has established Your Highness—how can his benevolence and depth be measured!"

sentences.zh: 臣願大王事之，敬之，政事壹聽之，大王垂拱南面而已。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Highness to serve him, revere him, and in all government affairs heed him entirely—Your Highness need only sit with folded hands facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant wishes Your Highness to serve him, revere him, and in all government affairs heed him entirely—Your Highness need only sit with folded hands facing south."

sentences.zh: 願留意，常以為念！

translations.literal: I beg you to keep this in mind and often make it your thought!
translations.idiomatic: Keep this in mind and often make it your thought!"

sentences.zh: 王至濟陽，求長鳴雞，道買積竹杖。

translations.literal: The prince reached Jiyang, sought long-crowing cocks, and along the road bought tall bamboo staffs.
translations.idiomatic: The prince reached Jiyang, sought long-crowing cocks, and along the road bought tall bamboo staffs.

sentences.zh: 過弘農，使大奴善以衣車載女子。

translations.literal: Passing Hongnong, he had his great slave Shan use a curtained carriage to carry women.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Hongnong, he had his great slave Shan use a curtained carriage to carry women.

sentences.zh: 至湖，使者以讓相安樂。

translations.literal: Reaching Hu, the envoy reproached Chancellor Anle.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Hu, the envoy reproached Chancellor Anle.

sentences.zh: 安樂告龔遂，遂入問王，王曰：「無有。

translations.literal: Anle told Gong Sui; Sui entered and questioned the prince. The prince said: "There was nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Anle told Gong Sui; Sui entered and questioned the prince. The prince said, "There was nothing."

sentences.zh: 」遂曰：「即無有，何愛一善以毀行義！

translations.literal: " Sui said: "If there was nothing, why spare one Shan and ruin righteous conduct!
translations.idiomatic: " Sui said, "If there was nothing, why spare one Shan and ruin righteous conduct!"

sentences.zh: 請收屬吏，以湔灑大王。

translations.literal: I ask to take him into custody and hand him to the officials, to cleanse Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to take him into custody and hand him to the officials, to cleanse Your Highness."

sentences.zh: 」即捽善屬衛士長行法。

translations.literal: " He at once seized Shan and handed him to the captain of the guards for punishment according to law.
translations.idiomatic: " He at once seized Shan and handed him to the captain of the guards for punishment according to law.

sentences.zh: 王到霸上，大鴻臚郊迎，騶奉乘輿車。

translations.literal: When the prince reached Bashang, the Grand Herald met him in suburban welcome; grooms presented the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince reached Bashang, the Grand Herald met him in suburban welcome; grooms presented the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 王使壽成御，郎中令遂參乘。

translations.literal: The prince had Shoucheng drive; the Director of the Gentlemen Sui rode as attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The prince had Shoucheng drive; Director of the Gentlemen Sui rode as attendant.

sentences.zh: 且至廣明、東都門，遂曰：「禮，奔喪望見國都哭。

translations.literal: As they neared Guangming and the East Capital Gate, Sui said: "By ritual, when hurrying to a funeral one weeps on sight of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: As they neared Guangming and the East Capital Gate, Sui said, "By ritual, when hurrying to a funeral one weeps on sight of the capital."

sentences.zh: 此長安東郭門也。

translations.literal: This is the eastern outer gate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: This is the eastern outer gate of Chang'an."

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「我嗌痛，不能哭。

translations.literal: " The prince said: "My throat hurts; I cannot weep.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince said, "My throat hurts; I cannot weep."

sentences.zh: 」至城門，遂復言，王曰：「城門與郭門等耳。

translations.literal: " Reaching the city gate, Sui spoke again; the prince said: "The city gate and the outer gate are the same.
translations.idiomatic: " Reaching the city gate, Sui spoke again; the prince said, "The city gate and the outer gate are the same."

sentences.zh: 」且至未央宮東闕，遂曰：「昌邑帳在是闕外馳道北，未至帳所，有南北行道，馬足未至數步；

translations.literal: " As they neared the eastern tower of Weiyang Palace, Sui said: "The Changyi quarters lie north of the imperial roadway outside this tower. Before reaching the quarters there is a north-south lane; when the horse's hooves are still several paces short;
translations.idiomatic: " As they neared the eastern tower of Weiyang Palace, Sui said, "The Changyi quarters lie north of the imperial roadway outside this tower. Before reaching the quarters there is a north-south lane; when the horse's hooves are still several paces short;"

sentences.zh: 大王宜下車，鄉闕西面伏哭，盡哀止。

translations.literal: Your Highness ought to descend from the carriage, turn toward the tower and prostrate yourself weeping to the west, exhausting grief and then stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness ought to descend, turn toward the tower and prostrate yourself weeping to the west, exhaust your grief, and then stop."

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「諾。

translations.literal: " The prince said: "Yes.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince said, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 」到，哭如儀。

translations.literal: " On arrival he wept according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: " On arrival he wept according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙寅，王受皇帝璽綬，襲尊號，尊皇后曰皇太后。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on bingyin, the prince received the imperial seal and ribbon, assumed the exalted title, and honored the empress as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on bingyin, the prince received the imperial seal and ribbon, assumed the exalted title, and honored the empress as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: ----3壬申，葬孝昭皇帝於平陵。

translations.literal: ----3 On renshen, Emperor Xiao of Zhao was buried at Pingling.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 On renshen, Emperor Xiao of Zhao was buried at Pingling.

sentences.zh: ----4昌邑王既立，淫戲無度。

translations.literal: ----4 Once the Prince of Changyi was established, his lewd sport knew no bounds.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 Once Prince He of Changyi was established, his lewd sport knew no bounds.

sentences.zh: 昌邑官屬皆徵至長安，往往超擢拜官。

translations.literal: Changyi officials and retainers were all summoned to Chang'an and were often promoted and enfeoffed beyond their rank.
translations.idiomatic: Changyi officials and retainers were all summoned to Chang'an and were often promoted and enfeoffed beyond their rank.

sentences.zh: 相安樂遷長樂衛尉。

translations.literal: Chancellor Anle was transferred to Commandant of the Guards for Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Anle was transferred to Commandant of the Guards for Changle.

sentences.zh: 龔遂見安樂，流涕謂曰：「王立為天子，日益驕溢，諫之不復聽。

translations.literal: Gong Sui saw Anle, wept, and said: "The prince has been made Son of Heaven and daily grows more arrogant and excessive; he no longer heeds admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Sui saw Anle, wept, and said, "The prince has been made Son of Heaven and daily grows more arrogant and excessive; he no longer heeds admonition."

sentences.zh: 今哀痛未盡，日與近臣飲酒作樂，鬥虎豹，召皮軒車九旒，驅馳東西，所為悖道。

translations.literal: Now mourning grief is not yet exhausted, yet day by day he drinks and makes sport with close retainers, pits tigers and leopards in combat, summons the nine-tassel leather-canopied chariot, and gallops east and west—his acts violate the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning grief is not yet exhausted, yet day by day he drinks and makes sport with close retainers, pits tigers and leopards in combat, summons the nine-tassel leather-canopied chariot, and gallops east and west—his acts violate the Way."

sentences.zh: 古制寬，大臣有隱退；

translations.literal: Ancient institutions were broad; great ministers might withdraw in concealment;
translations.idiomatic: Ancient institutions were broad; great ministers might withdraw in concealment;"

sentences.zh: 今去不得，陽狂恐知，身死為世戮，奈何？

translations.literal: now to leave is not permitted; feigning madness for fear of being known, one's body dies and becomes the world's disgrace—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: now to leave is not permitted; feigning madness for fear of being known, one's body dies and becomes the world's disgrace—what is to be done?"

sentences.zh: 君，陛下故相，宜極諫爭。

translations.literal: You, my lord, were the emperor's former chancellor; you ought to remonstrate to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: You, my lord, were the emperor's former chancellor; you ought to remonstrate to the utmost."

sentences.zh: 王夢青蠅之矢積西階東，可五六石，以屋版瓦覆之，以問遂，遂曰：「陛下之《詩》不雲乎：『營營青蠅，止於籓。

translations.literal: The emperor dreamed that green fly droppings piled east of the western stair, some five or six piculs, covered with roof tiles; he asked Sui. Sui said: "Does not Your Majesty's Odes say: 'Buzzing green flies stop at the fence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dreamed that green fly droppings piled east of the western stair, some five or six piculs, covered with roof tiles; he asked Sui. Sui said, "Does not Your Majesty's Odes say, 'Buzzing green flies stop at the fence."

sentences.zh: 愷悌君子，毋信讒言。

translations.literal: Easy and gracious is the gentleman—do not trust slanderous words.
translations.idiomatic: Easy and gracious is the gentleman—do not trust slanderous words."

sentences.zh: 』陛下左側讒人眾多，如是青蠅惡矣。

translations.literal: ' Slanderers at Your Majesty's left are many; such are the green flies' evil.
translations.idiomatic: ' Slanderers at Your Majesty's left are many—such is the evil of green flies."

sentences.zh: 宜進先帝大臣子孫，親近以為左右。

translations.literal: You ought to advance the sons and grandsons of the former emperor's great ministers and draw them near as those at your side.
translations.idiomatic: You ought to advance the sons and grandsons of the former emperor's great ministers and draw them near as those at your side."

sentences.zh: 如不忍昌邑故人，信用讒諛，必有凶咎。

translations.literal: If you cannot bear to part with old Changyi associates and trust slander and flattery, there will surely be misfortune and calamity.
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot bear to part with your old Changyi associates and trust slander and flattery, disaster is sure to follow.

sentences.zh: 願詭禍為福，皆放逐之！

translations.literal: I wish to turn misfortune into fortune—all should be banished!
translations.idiomatic: Turn misfortune into fortune—banish them all!

sentences.zh: 臣當先逐矣。

translations.literal: Your servant ought to be the first expelled.
translations.idiomatic: I ought to be the first one expelled.

sentences.zh: 」王不聽。

translations.literal: " The king would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " The king would not listen.

sentences.zh: 太僕丞河東張敞上書諫，曰：「孝昭皇帝蚤崩無嗣，大臣憂懼，選賢聖承宗廟，東迎之日，唯恐屬車之行遲。

translations.literal: Director of Studs Assistant Zhang Chang of Hedong submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying: "Emperor Xiao of filial piety died early without heir; great ministers were anxious and fearful, selected the worthy and sage to succeed the ancestral temple. On the day of welcoming from the east, all feared the train of the imperial carriage would be delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Studs Assistant Zhang Chang of Hedong submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying, "Emperor Zhao died young without an heir; the great ministers were anxious and fearful and selected a worthy man to succeed the ancestral temple. On the day of welcoming him from the east, everyone feared the imperial procession would be delayed.

sentences.zh: 今天子以盛年初即位，天下莫不拭目傾耳，觀化聽風。

translations.literal: Now the Son of Heaven at a flourishing age has first taken the throne; all under Heaven none do not wipe their eyes and incline their ears, observing transformation and listening to the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor has just taken the throne in the prime of youth, and all under Heaven watches with eager eyes and ears for signs of reform.

sentences.zh: 國輔大臣未褒，而昌邑小輩先遷，此過之大者也。

translations.literal: State-supporting great ministers have not yet been rewarded, yet Changyi petty men are promoted first—this is among the greatest of faults.
translations.idiomatic: The great ministers who support the state have not yet been rewarded, while petty men from Changyi are promoted first—this is a grave fault indeed.

sentences.zh: 」王不聽。

translations.literal: " The king would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " The king would not listen.

sentences.zh: 大將軍光憂懣，獨以問所親故吏大司農田延年。

translations.literal: Grand General Guang was distressed and resentful and alone took counsel with his close old subordinate Grand Minister of Agriculture Tian Yannian.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Huo Guang was distressed and resentful and confided only in his close old subordinate, Grand Minister of Agriculture Tian Yannian.

sentences.zh: 延年曰：「將軍為國柱石，審此人不可，何不建白太后，更選賢而立之？

translations.literal: Yannian said: "The general is the state's pillar and cornerstone; having examined that this man will not do, why not present a memorial to the Empress Dowager, select again the worthy, and establish him?
translations.idiomatic: Yannian said, "General, you are the pillar of the state. Having judged this man unfit, why not report to the Empress Dowager, choose another worthy man, and enthrone him?

sentences.zh: 」光曰：「今欲如是，於古嘗有此不？

translations.literal: " Guang said: "If we now wish to act thus, was there ever such a thing in antiquity?"
translations.idiomatic: " Guang said, "If we wish to act thus now, was there ever such a thing in antiquity?"

sentences.zh: 」延年曰：「伊尹相殷，廢太甲以安宗廟，後世稱其忠。

translations.literal: " Yannian said: "Yi Yin served as minister of Yin, deposed Tai Jia to secure the ancestral temple, and later ages praised his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: " Yannian said, "Yi Yin served Yin, deposed Tai Jia to secure the ancestral temple, and later ages praised his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 將軍若能行此，亦漢之伊尹也。

translations.literal: If the general can carry this out, he too will be the Yi Yin of Han.
translations.idiomatic: If the general can do this, you will be Han's Yi Yin as well.

sentences.zh: 」光乃引延年給事中，陰與車騎將軍張安世圖計。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Guang brought Yannian in as Palace Attendant and secretly with Cavalry-and-Chariots General Zhang Anshi plotted the plan.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Guang brought Yannian in as Palace Attendant and secretly plotted with Cavalry-and-Chariots General Zhang Anshi.

sentences.zh: 王出遊，光祿大夫魯國夏侯勝當乘輿前諫曰：「天久陰而不雨，臣下有謀上者。

translations.literal: The king went out touring; Palace Illustrious Grandee Xia Hou Sheng of Lu State, who should remonstrate before the imperial carriage, said: "Heaven has long been overcast without rain—among the ministers below there are those plotting against their superior.
translations.idiomatic: When the king went out touring, Palace Illustrious Grandee Xia Hou Sheng of Lu, whose duty was to remonstrate before the imperial carriage, said, "Heaven has long been overcast without rain—among the ministers below there are those plotting against their superior.

sentences.zh: 陛下出，欲何之？

translations.literal: Your Majesty goes forth—whither do you wish to go?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is going out—where do you intend to go?

sentences.zh: 」王怒，謂勝為示夭言，縛以屬吏。

translations.literal: " The king was angry, called Sheng's words inauspicious speech, bound him, and handed him over to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: " The king was angry, called Sheng's words inauspicious, bound him, and handed him over to the officials for punishment.

sentences.zh: 吏白霍光，光不舉法。

translations.literal: The officials reported to Huo Guang; Guang did not enforce the law.
translations.idiomatic: The officials reported to Huo Guang, but Guang did not enforce the law.

sentences.zh: 光讓安世，以為洩語。

translations.literal: Guang reproached Anshi, thinking he had leaked their words.
translations.idiomatic: Guang reproached Anshi, thinking he had leaked their plan.

sentences.zh: 安世實不言；

translations.literal: Anshi in truth had not spoken;
translations.idiomatic: Anshi had in truth said nothing;

sentences.zh: 乃召問勝。

translations.literal: thereupon he summoned and questioned Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: so he summoned and questioned Sheng.

sentences.zh: 勝對言：「在《鴻範傳》曰：『皇之不極，厥罰常陰，時則有下人伐上者。

translations.literal: Sheng replied, saying: "In the Hong Fan Commentary it says: 'When the Sovereign lacks the utmost, its punishment is constant yin; at such times there are inferiors who attack their superior.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng replied, "The Hong Fan Commentary says, 'When the Sovereign lacks the utmost, the punishment is constant overcast skies; at such times inferiors attack their superiors.

sentences.zh: 』惡察察言，故云『臣下有謀』。

translations.literal: ' I dislike overly explicit speech, therefore I said 'among the ministers below there is plotting.'"
translations.idiomatic: ' I dislike overly explicit speech, therefore I said 'among the ministers below there is plotting.'"

sentences.zh: 」光、安世大驚，以此益重經術士。

translations.literal: " Guang and Anshi were greatly alarmed and for this reason valued classicist scholars all the more.
translations.idiomatic: " Guang and Anshi were greatly alarmed and for this reason valued classicist scholars all the more.

sentences.zh: 侍中傅嘉數進諫，王亦縛嘉繫獄。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Fu Jia repeatedly advanced remonstrance; the king also bound Jia and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Fu Jia repeatedly remonstrated; the king also bound Jia and put him in prison.

sentences.zh: 光、安世既定議，乃使田延年報丞相楊敞。

translations.literal: Once Guang and Anshi had settled their decision, they sent Tian Yannian to inform Chancellor Yang Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Once Guang and Anshi had settled their decision, they sent Tian Yannian to inform Chancellor Yang Chang.

sentences.zh: 敞驚懼，不知所言，汗出洽背，徒唯唯而已。

translations.literal: Chang was alarmed and fearful, not knowing what to say; sweat poured soaking his back—he only murmured assent.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was alarmed and at a loss for words; sweat soaked his back and he could only murmur assent.

sentences.zh: 延年起，至更衣，敞夫人遽從東廂謂敞曰：「此國大事，今大將軍議已定，使九卿來報君侯，君侯不疾應，與大將軍同心，猶與無決，先事誅矣！

translations.literal: Yannian rose and went to the side chamber; Chancellor Chang's wife hastily from the east wing said to Chang: "This is a great affair of state. Now the Grand General's deliberation is settled and he sent the Nine Ministers to report to you, my lord. If you, my lord, do not respond swiftly and are of one heart with the Grand General, it is as if there were no resolution—you will be executed first!
translations.idiomatic: Yannian rose and went to the side chamber; Chancellor Chang's wife hastened from the east wing and said to him, "This is a matter of state. The Grand General's plan is settled and he has sent the Nine Ministers to report to you. If you do not respond swiftly and stand with the Grand General, it is as good as having no resolution—you will be the first executed!

sentences.zh: 」延年從更衣還，敞夫人與延年參語許諾：「請奉大將軍教令！

translations.literal: " When Yannian returned from the side chamber, Chancellor Chang's wife and Yannian spoke together in assent: "We request to follow the Grand General's command!
translations.idiomatic: " When Yannian returned from the side chamber, Chancellor Chang's wife and Yannian spoke together in assent, "We shall follow the Grand General's command!

sentences.zh: 癸巳，光召丞相、御史、將軍、列侯、中二千石、大夫、博士會議未央宮。

translations.literal: On guisi, Guang summoned the chancellor, censor, generals, ranked marquises, officials of middle two thousand dan, grandees, and erudites to deliberate in Weiyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Guang summoned the chancellor, censor, generals, ranked marquises, officials of middle two thousand dan rank, grandees, and erudites to meet in Weiyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 光曰：「昌邑王行昏亂，恐危社稷，如何？

translations.literal: Guang said: "The King of Changyi's conduct is benighted and chaotic—I fear he endangers the altars of soil and grain. What is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Guang said, "The King of Changyi's conduct is benighted and chaotic and I fear he endangers the state. What is to be done?"

sentences.zh: 」群臣皆驚鄂失色，莫敢發言，但唯唯而已。

translations.literal: " The assembled ministers were all startled speechless, faces changed color, none dared speak—they only murmured assent.
translations.idiomatic: " The assembled ministers were all startled speechless, their faces drained of color; none dared speak and could only murmur assent.

sentences.zh: 田延年前，離席按劍曰：「先帝屬將軍以幼孤，寄將軍以天下，以將軍忠賢，能安劉氏也。

translations.literal: Tian Yannian stepped forward, left his seat, and hand on sword said: "The former emperor entrusted the general with the young orphan and committed all under Heaven to the general, because the general is loyal and worthy and can secure the house of Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yannian stepped forward, left his seat, and with hand on sword said, "The late emperor entrusted you, General, with the young orphan and committed the realm to you because you are loyal and worthy and can secure the house of Liu.

sentences.zh: 今群下鼎沸，社稷將傾；

translations.literal: Now the assembled ministers boil like a cauldron and the altars of soil and grain are about to topple;
translations.idiomatic: Now the court boils like a cauldron and the state is about to topple;

sentences.zh: 且漢之傳謚常為『孝』者，以長有天下，令宗廟血食也。

translations.literal: moreover among Han's transmitted posthumous titles those regularly bearing 'Filial' do so because they long held all under Heaven and let the ancestral temple receive blood sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: moreover among Han's posthumous titles those bearing 'Filial' earned it by long holding the realm and keeping the ancestral sacrifices alive.

sentences.zh: 如漢家絕祀，將軍雖死，何面目見先帝於地下乎？

translations.literal: If the house of Han's sacrifices are cut off, though the general die, with what face could he meet the former emperor below ground?
translations.idiomatic: If the house of Han's sacrifices end, General, even in death with what face could you meet the late emperor in the underworld?

sentences.zh: 今日之議，不得旋踵，群臣後應者，臣請劍斬之！

translations.literal: Today's deliberation brooks no turning of the heel; any minister who responds afterward—I request to cut him down with the sword!
translations.idiomatic: Today's deliberation brooks no delay; any minister who responds afterward—I ask to cut him down with the sword!

sentences.zh: 」光謝曰：「九卿責光是也！

translations.literal: " Guang apologized, saying: "The Nine Ministers rightly reproach Guang!
translations.idiomatic: " Guang apologized, saying, "The Nine Ministers rightly reproach me!

sentences.zh: 天下匈匈不安，光當受難。

translations.literal: All under Heaven is restive and unsettled; Guang ought to bear the hardship.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven is restless and unsettled; I ought to bear the hardship.

sentences.zh: 」於是議者皆叩頭曰：「萬姓之命，在於將軍，唯大將軍令！

translations.literal: " Thereupon the deliberators all kowtowed, saying: "The myriad people's lives rest on the general—we await only the Grand General's command!
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon all present kowtowed, saying, "The lives of the myriad people rest on the General—we await only the Grand General's command!

sentences.zh: 光即與群臣俱見，白太后，具陳昌邑王不可以承宗廟狀。

translations.literal: Guang immediately together with the assembled ministers went to audience, reported to the Empress Dowager, and fully set forth the King of Changyi's condition unfit to succeed the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Guang immediately went with the assembled ministers to audience, reported to the Empress Dowager, and fully set forth why the King of Changyi could not succeed the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 皇太后乃車駕幸未央承明殿，詔諸禁門毋內昌邑群臣。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager thereupon took her carriage and visited Weiyang's Chengming Hall and edicted that at all forbidden gates none should admit Changyi ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager thereupon took her carriage to Chengming Hall in Weiyang Palace and edicted that at all forbidden gates Changyi ministers were not to be admitted.

sentences.zh: 王入朝太后還，乘輦欲歸溫室。

translations.literal: The king entered to attend the Empress Dowager and returned, mounted the palanquin, and wished to return to the Warm Apartment.
translations.idiomatic: The king had attended the Empress Dowager and returned, mounted his palanquin, and wished to return to the Warm Apartment.

sentences.zh: 中黃門宦者各持門扇，王入，門閉，昌邑群臣不得入。

translations.literal: Central Yellow Gate eunuchs each held the gate leaves; the king entered, the gates closed, and Changyi ministers could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Central Yellow Gate eunuchs each held the gate panels; when the king entered the gates closed and the Changyi ministers could not follow.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「何為？

translations.literal: The king said: "What is this for?"
translations.idiomatic: The king said, "What is going on?"

sentences.zh: 」大將軍跪曰：「有皇太后詔，毋內昌邑群臣！

translations.literal: " The Grand General knelt and said: "There is an edict of the Empress Dowager—do not admit Changyi ministers!"
translations.idiomatic: " The Grand General knelt and said, "There is an edict of the Empress Dowager—do not admit the Changyi ministers!"

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「徐之，何乃驚人如是！

translations.literal: " The king said: "Take it slowly—why startle people so!"
translations.idiomatic: " The king said, "Take it slowly—why startle people like this!"

sentences.zh: 」光使盡驅出昌邑群臣，置金馬門外。

translations.literal: " Guang had all Changyi ministers driven out and placed outside the Golden Horse Gate.
translations.idiomatic: " Guang had all the Changyi ministers driven out and placed outside the Golden Horse Gate.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍安世將羽林騎，收縛二百餘人，皆送廷尉詔獄。

translations.literal: Cavalry-and-Chariots General Anshi led Feathered Forest cavalry, seized and bound more than two hundred men, and all were sent to the Commandant of Justice's imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry-and-Chariots General Anshi led Feathered Forest cavalry, seized and bound more than two hundred men, and sent them all to the imperial prison under the Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 令故昭帝侍中中臣侍守王。

translations.literal: He ordered the former Emperor Zhao's palace attendants and inner attendants to attend and guard the king.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Emperor Zhao's former palace attendants and inner attendants to attend and guard the king.

sentences.zh: 光敕左右：「謹宿衛！

translations.literal: Guang charged those at hand: "Guard carefully!
translations.idiomatic: Guang charged those at hand, "Guard carefully!

sentences.zh: 卒有物故自裁，令我負天下，有殺主名。

translations.literal: If he should suddenly die by suicide, it would make me bear guilt under Heaven and have the reputation of regicide.
translations.idiomatic: If he should suddenly die by suicide, I would bear guilt under Heaven and have the name of regicide.

sentences.zh: 」王尚未自知當廢，謂左右：「我故群臣從官安得罪，而大將軍盡系之乎！

translations.literal: " The king did not yet know himself about to be deposed and said to those at hand: "How have my old ministers and followers offended, that the Grand General binds them all!"
translations.idiomatic: " The king did not yet know he was about to be deposed and said to those at hand, "How have my old ministers and followers offended that the Grand General binds them all!"

sentences.zh: 頃之，有太后詔召王。

translations.literal: Before long there was an edict of the Empress Dowager summoning the king.
translations.idiomatic: Before long came an edict of the Empress Dowager summoning the king.

sentences.zh: 王聞召，意恐，乃曰：「我安得罪而召我哉！

translations.literal: The king heard the summons, his mind fearful, and said: "How have I offended that I am summoned!"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the summons, the king grew fearful and said, "How have I offended that I am summoned!"

sentences.zh: 」太后被珠襦，盛服坐武帳中，侍御數百人皆持兵，期門武士陛戟陳列殿下，群臣以次上殿，召昌邑王伏前聽詔。

translations.literal: " The Empress Dowager wore a pearl-lined jacket and full regalia, seated in the martial canopy; several hundred attendants all held weapons; Barrier Gate warriors with halberds on the steps arrayed below the hall; the assembled ministers in order ascended the hall—the King of Changyi was summoned to prostrate before and hear the edict.
translations.idiomatic: " The Empress Dowager wore a pearl-lined jacket and full court dress, seated in the martial canopy; several hundred attendants all held weapons; Barrier Gate warriors with halberds on the steps lined the hall below; the assembled ministers ascended in order, and the King of Changyi was summoned to prostrate and hear the edict.

sentences.zh: 光與群臣連名奏王，尚書令讀奏曰：「丞相臣敞等昧死言皇太后陛下：孝昭皇帝早棄天下，遣使徵昌邑王典喪，服斬衰，無悲哀之心，廢禮誼，居道上不素食，使從官略女子載衣車，內所居傳捨。

translations.literal: Guang together with the assembled ministers jointly memorialized the king; the Director of the Masters of Writing read the memorial, saying: "Chancellor your servant Chang and others, risking death, speak to Her Majesty the Empress Dowager: Emperor Xiao early abandoned all under Heaven; envoys were sent to summon the King of Changyi to preside over the mourning. He wore hemp mourning with frayed edges yet had no heart of grief, discarded ritual and propriety, while on the road did not eat vegetarian mourning food, had followers abduct women into clothing carts, and brought them within the relay lodges where he lodged.
translations.idiomatic: Guang and the assembled ministers jointly memorialized the king; the Director of the Masters of Writing read the memorial, saying, "Chancellor Yang Chang and others, risking death, address Her Majesty the Empress Dowager: Emperor Zhao died young; envoys were sent to summon the King of Changyi to preside over the mourning. He wore frayed-edge hemp mourning yet had no heart of grief, discarded ritual and propriety, ate no mourning vegetarian food on the road, had followers seize women into clothing carts, and brought them into the relay lodges where he stayed.

sentences.zh: 始至謁見，立為皇太子，常私買雞豚以食。

translations.literal: When he first arrived for audience he was established as heir apparent, yet constantly in private bought chickens and pigs to eat.
translations.idiomatic: When he first arrived for audience he was made heir apparent, yet constantly bought chickens and pigs in private to eat.

sentences.zh: 受皇帝信璽、行璽大行前，就次，發璽不封。

translations.literal: He received the emperor's credential seal and traveling seal before the Grand Procession, took his place, and opened the seals without resealing them.
translations.idiomatic: He received the emperor's credential seal and traveling seal before the Grand Procession, took his place, and opened the seals without resealing them.

sentences.zh: 從官更持節引內昌邑從官、騶宰、官奴二百餘人，常與居禁闥內敖戲。

translations.literal: Followers again held staffs of office and led in more than two hundred Changyi followers, outrider stewards, and official slaves, who constantly dwelt with him inside the forbidden inner gates sporting and playing.
translations.idiomatic: Followers again held staffs of office and led in more than two hundred Changyi followers, outrider stewards, and official slaves, who constantly lived with him inside the forbidden inner gates sporting and playing.

sentences.zh: 為書曰：『皇帝問侍中君卿：使中御府令高昌奉黃金千斤，賜君卿取十妻。

translations.literal: He made a letter saying: 'The emperor inquires of Palace Attendant Junqing: I order the Director of the Inner Palace Treasury Gao Chang to present a thousand jin of gold and bestow on Junqing permission to take ten wives.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a letter saying, 'The emperor inquires of Palace Attendant Junqing: I order Director of the Inner Palace Treasury Gao Chang to present a thousand jin of gold and bestow on Junqing permission to take ten wives.

sentences.zh: 』大行在前殿，發樂府樂器，引內昌邑樂人擊鼓，歌吹，作俳倡；

translations.literal: ' Before the front hall of the Grand Procession he issued music-office instruments, led in Changyi musicians to beat drums, sing and blow pipes, and perform comic entertainers;
translations.idiomatic: ' Before the front hall of the Grand Procession he issued music-office instruments, brought in Changyi musicians to beat drums, sing and play pipes, and perform comic entertainers;

sentences.zh: 召內泰壹、宗廟樂人，悉奏眾樂。

translations.literal: he summoned inner Grand Unity and ancestral-temple musicians and had them all perform the full music.
translations.idiomatic: he summoned inner Grand Unity and ancestral-temple musicians and had them all perform the full repertoire.

sentences.zh: 駕法駕驅馳北宮、桂宮，弄彘鬥虎。

translations.literal: He drove the imperial regalia carriage racing through Northern Palace and Cassia Palace, sporting with pigs and fighting tigers.
translations.idiomatic: He drove the imperial regalia carriage racing through the Northern Palace and Cassia Palace, sporting with pigs and fighting tigers.

sentences.zh: 召皇太后御小馬車，使官奴騎乘，遊戲掖庭中。

translations.literal: He summoned the Empress Dowager's small horse carriage, had official slaves mount and ride, and sported in the Rear Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the Empress Dowager's small horse carriage, had official slaves mount and ride it, and sported in the Rear Palace.

sentences.zh: 與孝昭皇帝宮人蒙等淫亂，詔掖庭令：『敢洩言，要斬！

translations.literal: With Emperor Xiao's palace women Meng and the rest he committed lewd disorder and edicted the Rear Palace director: 'Whoever dares leak word—beheading at the waist!
translations.idiomatic: With Emperor Zhao's palace women Meng and the rest he committed lewd disorder and edicted the Rear Palace director, 'Whoever dares leak word shall be beheaded at the waist!

translations.literal: ' ……" The Empress Dowager said: "Stop!"
translations.idiomatic: ' ……" The Empress Dowager said, "Stop!"

sentences.zh: 為人臣子，當悖亂如是邪！

translations.literal: As a man's minister and son, ought he be so perverse and chaotic!
translations.idiomatic: As subject and son, ought he be so perverse and chaotic!

sentences.zh: 」王離席伏。

translations.literal: " The king left his seat and prostrated himself.
translations.idiomatic: " The king left his seat and prostrated himself.

sentences.zh: 尚書令復讀曰：「……取諸侯王、列侯、二千石綬及墨綬、黃綬以並佩昌邑郎官者免奴。

translations.literal: The Director of the Masters of Writing again read: "…… He took marquises of kingdoms, ranked marquises, and two-thousand-dan ribbons together with black and yellow ribbons and had them all worn together by Changyi gentlemen-at-attendance to free slaves.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Masters of Writing read again, "…… He took the ribbons of kings, marquises, and two-thousand-dan officials together with black and yellow ribbons and had Changyi gentlemen-at-attendance wear them together to free slaves.

sentences.zh: 發御府金錢、刀劍、玉器、采繒，賞賜所與遊戲者。

translations.literal: He issued imperial treasury gold and cash, swords, jade objects, and colored silks, bestowing them on those with whom he sported.
translations.idiomatic: He issued imperial treasury gold, cash, swords, jade objects, and colored silks and bestowed them on his playmates.

sentences.zh: 與從官、官奴夜飲，湛沔於酒。

translations.literal: With followers and official slaves he drank by night, steeped to the brim in wine.
translations.idiomatic: With followers and official slaves he drank by night, steeped in wine.

sentences.zh: 獨夜設九賓溫室，延見姊夫昌邑關內侯。

translations.literal: Alone at night he set out nine-guest reception in the Warm Apartment and extended audience to his brother-in-law, Marquis within the Passes of Changyi.
translations.idiomatic: Alone at night he held nine-guest reception in the Warm Apartment and received his brother-in-law, Marquis within the Passes of Changyi.

sentences.zh: 祖宗廟祠未舉，為璽書，使使者持節以三太牢祠昌邑哀王園廟，稱『嗣子皇帝』。

translations.literal: Ancestral temple sacrifices had not yet been performed; he made a sealed letter and sent envoys holding staffs of office with triple grand sacrificial victims to sacrifice at the park temple of the Lamented King of Changyi, styling himself 'heir-son emperor.'
translations.idiomatic: Ancestral temple sacrifices had not yet been performed; he made a sealed letter and sent envoys with staffs of office and triple grand sacrificial victims to sacrifice at the park temple of the Lamented King of Changyi, styling himself 'heir-son emperor.'

sentences.zh: 受璽以來二十七日，使者旁午，持節詔諸官署徵發凡一千一百二十七事。

translations.literal: From receiving the seal to the present twenty-seven days, envoys crisscrossed, holding staffs of office to edict all offices for requisitions and issuances—in all one thousand one hundred twenty-seven matters.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seven days since receiving the seal, envoys crisscrossed constantly, holding staffs of office to edict all offices for requisitions and issuances—in all one thousand one hundred twenty-seven matters.

sentences.zh: 荒淫迷惑，失帝王禮誼，亂漢制度。

translations.literal: Dissolute, lewd, and deluded, he lost the Son of Heaven's ritual and propriety and threw Han's institutions into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Dissolute, lewd, and deluded, he abandoned imperial ritual and propriety and threw Han institutions into disorder.

sentences.zh: 臣敞等數進諫，不變更，日以益甚。

translations.literal: Your servants Chang and the rest repeatedly advanced remonstrance; he did not change, and daily it grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: We repeatedly remonstrated; he did not change, and daily grew worse.

sentences.zh: 恐危社稷，天下不安。

translations.literal: We fear he endangers the altars of soil and grain and all under Heaven is unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: We fear he endangers the state and all under Heaven is unsettled.

sentences.zh: 臣敞等謹與博士議，皆曰：『今陛下嗣孝昭皇帝後，行淫辟不軌。

translations.literal: Your servants Chang and the rest respectfully deliberated with the erudites; all said: 'Now Your Majesty succeeds Emperor Xiao and conducts lewd depravity not according to the norm.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully deliberated with the erudites; all said, 'Now Your Majesty succeeds Emperor Zhao and conducts lewd depravity contrary to the norm.

sentences.zh: 「五辟之屬，莫大不孝。

translations.literal: " Among the five serious offenses, none is greater than unfilial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: " Among the five serious offenses, none is greater than unfilial conduct.

sentences.zh: 」周襄王不能事母，《春秋》曰：「天王出居於鄭，」由不孝出之，絕之於天下也。

translations.literal: " King Xiang of Zhou could not serve his mother. The Spring and Autumn Annals says: 'The Son of Heaven went out to dwell at Zheng'—because of unfilial conduct he was sent out and cut off from all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " King Xiang of Zhou could not serve his mother. The Spring and Autumn Annals says, 'The Son of Heaven went out to dwell at Zheng'—because of unfilial conduct he was sent out and cut off from all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 宗廟重於君，陛下不可以承天序，奉祖宗廟，子萬姓，當廢！

translations.literal: The ancestral temple weighs heavier than the ruler; Your Majesty cannot succeed Heaven's succession, serve the ancestral temple, or be parent to the myriad people—you ought to be deposed!
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral temple weighs heavier than the ruler; Your Majesty cannot succeed Heaven's order, serve the ancestral temple, or be parent to the myriad people—you ought to be deposed!

sentences.zh: 』臣請有司以一太牢具告祠高廟。

translations.literal: ' Your servants request the responsible offices to report the sacrifice to the High Temple with one grand sacrificial victim.
translations.idiomatic: ' We request the responsible offices to report the sacrifice to the High Temple with one grand sacrificial victim.

sentences.zh: 」皇太后詔曰：「可。

translations.literal: " The Empress Dowager edicted: "Approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The Empress Dowager edicted, "Approved.

sentences.zh: 」光令王起，拜受詔，王曰：「聞『天下有爭臣七人，雖亡道不失天下。

translations.literal: " Guang ordered the king to rise and bow to receive the edict; the king said: "I have heard 'Under all under Heaven there are seven remonstrating ministers—even if without the Way one does not lose the realm.
translations.idiomatic: " Guang ordered the king to rise and bow to receive the edict; the king said, "I have heard, 'Under Heaven there are seven remonstrating ministers—even if without the Way one does not lose the realm.

sentences.zh: 』」光曰：「皇太后詔廢，安得稱天子！

translations.literal: '" Guang said: "The Empress Dowager has edicted deposal—how can you style yourself Son of Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: '" Guang said, "The Empress Dowager has edicted your deposition—how can you still call yourself Son of Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 」乃即持其手，解脫其璽組，奉上太后，扶王下殿，出金馬門，群臣隨送。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he immediately took his hand, removed his seal cord, presented it up to the Empress Dowager, supported the king down from the hall, and went out the Golden Horse Gate—the assembled ministers followed in escort.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he immediately took the king's hand, removed his seal cord, presented it to the Empress Dowager, supported the king down from the hall, and went out the Golden Horse Gate with the assembled ministers following in escort.

sentences.zh: 王西面拜曰：「愚戇，不任漢事！

translations.literal: The king faced west and bowed, saying: "Stupid and blunt—I am not fit for Han's affairs!
translations.idiomatic: The king faced west and bowed, saying, "Stupid and blunt—I am not fit for Han's affairs!

sentences.zh: 」起，就乘輿副車，大將軍光送至昌邑邸。

translations.literal: " He rose, mounted the palanquin's escort carriage, and Grand General Guang escorted him to the Changyi residence.
translations.idiomatic: " He rose, mounted the escort carriage of the palanquin, and Grand General Guang escorted him to the Changyi residence.

sentences.zh: 光謝曰：「王行自絕於天，臣寧負王，不敢負社稷！

translations.literal: Guang apologized, saying: "Your Majesty's conduct has cut itself off from Heaven; your servant would rather fail Your Majesty than fail the altars of soil and grain!
translations.idiomatic: Guang apologized, saying, "Your Majesty's conduct has cut itself off from Heaven; I would rather fail you than fail the state!

sentences.zh: 願王自愛，臣長不復左右。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to care for yourself; your servant will long not again be at your side.
translations.idiomatic: Take care of yourself, Your Majesty; I shall not again be at your side for long.

sentences.zh: 」光涕泣而去。

translations.literal: " Guang wept as he departed.
translations.idiomatic: " Guang wept as he departed.

sentences.zh: 群臣奏言：「古者廢放之人，屏於遠方，不及以政。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers memorialized, saying: "In antiquity deposed persons were screened off in distant regions and did not reach to government.
translations.idiomatic: The assembled ministers memorialized, saying, "In antiquity deposed persons were banished to distant regions and did not participate in government.

sentences.zh: 請徙王賀漢中房陵縣。

translations.literal: We request to relocate King He to Fangling County in Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: We request to relocate King He to Fangling County in Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 」太后詔歸賀昌邑，賜湯沐邑二千戶，故王家財物皆與賀；

translations.literal: " The Empress Dowager edicted to return He to Changyi, bestowed a bath-and-lodging fief of two thousand households, and all the former royal house's goods and property were given to He;
translations.idiomatic: " The Empress Dowager edicted to return He to Changyi, bestowed a bath fief of two thousand households, and gave him all the former royal house's goods and property;

sentences.zh: 及哀王女四人，各賜湯沐邑千戶；

translations.literal: and the Lamented King's four daughters each were bestowed bath fiefs of a thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: and the Lamented King's four daughters each received bath fiefs of a thousand households;

sentences.zh: 國除，為山陽郡。

translations.literal: the kingdom was abolished and made Shanyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: the kingdom was abolished and made Shanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 昌邑群臣坐在國時不舉奏王罪過，令漢朝不聞知，又不能輔道，陷王大惡，皆下獄，誅殺二百餘人。

translations.literal: Changyi ministers were convicted because while in the kingdom they did not memorialize the king's offenses and let the Han court not hear of them, and also could not assist and guide him, plunging the king into great wickedness—all were sent down to prison and more than two hundred were executed.
translations.idiomatic: The Changyi ministers were convicted because while in the kingdom they had not reported the king's offenses and let the Han court remain ignorant, and also failed to guide him, plunging the king into great wickedness—all were imprisoned and more than two hundred were executed.

sentences.zh: 唯中尉吉、郎中令遂以忠直數諫正，得減死，髡為城旦。

translations.literal: Only Commandant Ji and Director of the Palace Secretariat Sui, for loyal uprightness and repeatedly remonstrating and correcting, obtained reduced sentence from death and were shaved and made dawn wall-builders.
translations.idiomatic: Only Commandant Ji and Director of the Palace Secretariat Sui, for loyal uprightness and repeated remonstrance and correction, escaped death, were shaved, and sentenced to dawn wall-building labor.

sentences.zh: 師王式繫獄當死，治事使者責問曰：「師何以無諫書？

translations.literal: Teacher Wang Shi was imprisoned and liable to death; the investigating envoy reproached and questioned, saying: "Teacher, why are there no remonstrance memorials?"
translations.idiomatic: Teacher Wang Shi was imprisoned and liable to death; the investigating envoy questioned him, saying, "Teacher, why are there no remonstrance memorials?"

sentences.zh: 」式對曰：「臣以《詩》三百五篇朝夕授王，至於忠臣、孝子之篇，未嘗不為王反覆誦之也。

translations.literal: " Shi replied: "Your subject with the three hundred and five pieces of the Odes morning and evening instructs the king; as for the pieces on loyal ministers and filial sons, your subject has never failed to recite them repeatedly for the king.
translations.idiomatic: " Shi replied, "Your subject with the three hundred and five pieces of the Odes morning and evening instructs the king; as for the pieces on loyal ministers and filial sons, your subject has never failed to recite them repeatedly for the king.

sentences.zh: 至於危亡失道之君，未嘗不流涕為王深陳之也。

translations.literal: As for lords who were in peril, lost the Way, and perished, your subject has never failed to shed tears and for the king deeply set them forth.
translations.idiomatic: As for rulers who were in peril, lost the Way, and perished, your subject has never failed to shed tears and set them forth at length for the king.

sentences.zh: 臣以三百五篇諫，是以無諫書。

translations.literal: Your subject remonstrates with the three hundred and five pieces—therefore there is no remonstrance memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject remonstrates with the three hundred and five pieces—therefore there is no remonstrance memorial.

sentences.zh: 」使者以聞，亦得減死論。

translations.literal: " The envoy reported it; he also received a reduced-death sentence.
translations.idiomatic: " The envoy reported it; he also received a reduced-death sentence.

sentences.zh: 霍光以群臣奏事東宮，太后省政，宜知經術，白令夏侯勝用《尚書》授太后，遷勝長信少府，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Huo Guang, because the ministers presented affairs at the Eastern Palace and the empress dowager oversaw government, thought she should know the classics; he reported to have Xiahou Sheng use the Documents to instruct the empress dowager, moved Sheng to Chamberlain of Changxin, and granted the title Marquis within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Guang, because the ministers presented affairs at the Eastern Palace and the empress dowager oversaw government, thought she should know the classics; he reported to have Xiahou Sheng use the Documents to instruct the empress dowager, moved Sheng to Chamberlain of Changxin, and granted the title Marquis within the Passes.

sentences.zh: ----5初，衛太子納魯國史良娣，生子進，號史皇孫。

translations.literal: ----5 At the beginning, the Heir of Wei took as consort Lady Shi, a worthy lady of Lu, and bore a son Jin, styled the Shi Imperial Grandson.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 At the beginning, the Heir of Wei took as consort Lady Shi, a worthy lady of Lu, and bore a son Jin, styled the Shi Imperial Grandson.

sentences.zh: 皇孫納涿郡王夫人，生子病已，號皇曾孫。

translations.literal: The imperial grandson took as consort the Lady of Wang of Zhuo commandery and bore a son Bingyi, styled the Imperial Great-Grandson.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial grandson took as consort the Lady of Wang of Zhuo commandery and bore a son Bingyi, styled the Imperial Great-Grandson.

sentences.zh: 皇曾孫生數月，遭巫蠱事，太子三男、一女及諸妻、妾皆遇害，獨皇曾孫在，亦坐收系郡邸獄。

translations.literal: The imperial great-grandson was several months old when the witchcraft affair struck; the crown prince's three sons, one daughter, and all wives and concubines were harmed—only the imperial great-grandson remained, and he too was implicated, taken, and held in the commandery hostel prison.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial great-grandson was several months old when the witchcraft affair struck; the crown prince's three sons, one daughter, and all wives and concubines were harmed—only the imperial great-grandson remained, and he too was implicated, taken, and held in the commandery hostel prison.

sentences.zh: 故廷尉監魯國丙吉受詔治巫蠱獄，吉心知太子無事實，重哀皇曾孫無辜，擇謹厚女徒謂城胡組、淮陽郭徵卿，令乳養曾孫，置閒燥處。

translations.literal: Former Commandant of Justice Supervisor Bing Ji of Lu received an edict to try the witchcraft prison; Ji in his heart knew the crown prince had no factual guilt and deeply pitied the imperial great-grandson's innocence; he chose careful, solid female convicts named Cheng Huzu and Guo Zhengqing of Huaiyang, ordered them to nurse the great-grandson, and placed him in a quiet, dry place.
translations.idiomatic: Former Commandant of Justice Supervisor Bing Ji of Lu received an edict to try the witchcraft prison; Ji in his heart knew the crown prince had no factual guilt and deeply pitied the imperial great-grandson's innocence; he chose careful, solid female convicts named Cheng Huzu and Guo Zhengqing of Huaiyang, ordered them to nurse the great-grandson, and placed him in a quiet, dry place.

sentences.zh: 吉日再省視。

translations.literal: On auspicious days he again went to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: On auspicious days he again went to inspect.

sentences.zh: 巫蠱事連歲不決，武帝疾，來往長楊、五柞宮，望氣者言長安獄中有天子氣，於是武帝遣使者分條中都官，詔獄繫者，無輕重，一切皆殺之。

translations.literal: The witchcraft affair went unresolved for successive years; Emperor Wu was ill, coming and going between Changyang and Wuzuo palaces; qi-readers said there was Son-of-Heaven qi in Chang'an's prisons; thereupon Emperor Wu sent envoys to itemize separately the capital officials—those held in edict prisons, without regard to severity, all were to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: The witchcraft affair went unresolved for successive years; Emperor Wu was ill, coming and going between Changyang and Wuzuo palaces; qi-readers said there was Son-of-Heaven qi in Chang'an's prisons; thereupon Emperor Wu sent envoys to itemize separately the capital officials—those held in edict prisons, without regard to severity, all were to be killed.

sentences.zh: 內謁者令郭穰夜到郡邸獄，吉閉門拒使者不納，曰：「皇曾孫在。

translations.literal: Inner Usher-in-Chief Guo Rang came by night to the commandery hostel prison; Ji shut the gate, refused the envoy, and would not admit him, saying: "The imperial great-grandson is here.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Usher-in-Chief Guo Rang came by night to the commandery hostel prison; Ji shut the gate, refused the envoy, and would not admit him, saying, "The imperial great-grandson is here.

sentences.zh: 他人無辜死者猶不可，況親曾孫乎！

translations.literal: Others who died innocent still could not be allowed—how much more a close great-grandson!
translations.idiomatic: Others who died innocent still could not be allowed—how much more a close great-grandson!

sentences.zh: 」相守至天明，不得入。

translations.literal: " They held each other off until dawn; he could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: " They held each other off until dawn; he could not enter.

sentences.zh: 穰還，以聞，因劾奏吉。

translations.literal: Rang returned and reported it, and thereby impeached and memorialized Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Rang returned and reported it, and thereby impeached and memorialized Ji.

sentences.zh: 武帝亦寤，曰：「天使之也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu also awoke and said: "Heaven sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu also awoke and said, "Heaven sent him.

sentences.zh: 」因赦天下。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he amnestied all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he amnestied all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 郡邸獄繫者，獨賴吉得生。

translations.literal: Of those held in the commandery hostel prison, they alone relied on Ji to live.
translations.idiomatic: Of those held in the commandery hostel prison, they alone relied on Ji to live.

sentences.zh: 既而吉謂守丞誰如：「皇孫不當在官。

translations.literal: Afterward Ji told the prison warden Shei Ru: "The imperial grandson ought not to be in an office.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Ji told the prison warden Shei Ru, "The imperial grandson ought not to be in an office.

sentences.zh: 」使誰如移書京兆尹，遣與胡組俱送；

translations.literal: " He had Shei Ru send a letter to the Governor of Jingzhao to dispatch him together with Huzu;
translations.idiomatic: " He had Shei Ru send a letter to the Governor of Jingzhao to dispatch him together with Huzu;

sentences.zh: 京兆尹不受，復還。

translations.literal: the Governor of Jingzhao would not receive him, and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: the Governor of Jingzhao would not receive him, and he returned.

sentences.zh: 及組日滿當去，皇孫思慕，吉以私錢雇組令留，與郭徵卿並養，養月，乃遣組去。

translations.literal: When Huzu's term was full and she was to leave, the imperial grandson yearned for her; Ji with private money hired Huzu to stay; together with Guo Zhengqing they jointly nursed him; after a month of nursing he sent Huzu away.
translations.idiomatic: When Huzu's term was full and she was to leave, the imperial grandson yearned for her; Ji with private money hired Huzu to stay; together with Guo Zhengqing they jointly nursed him; after a month of nursing he sent Huzu away.

sentences.zh: 後少內嗇夫白吉曰：「食皇孫無詔令。

translations.literal: Later the junior palace provisioner reported to Ji: "Feeding the imperial grandson has no edict.
translations.idiomatic: Later the junior palace provisioner reported to Ji, "Feeding the imperial grandson has no edict.

sentences.zh: 」時吉得食米、肉，月月以給皇曾孫。

translations.literal: " At that time Ji obtained food, rice, and meat and month by month supplied the imperial great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Ji obtained food, rice, and meat and month by month supplied the imperial great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 曾孫病，幾不全者數焉，吉數敕保養乳母加致醫藥，視遇甚有恩惠。

translations.literal: The great-grandson fell ill and several times nearly did not survive; Ji repeatedly ordered the protectors and wet-nurses to add medicine, and his regard and treatment were very full of kindness.
translations.idiomatic: The great-grandson fell ill and several times nearly did not survive; Ji repeatedly ordered the protectors and wet-nurses to add medicine, and his regard and treatment were very full of kindness.

sentences.zh: 吉聞史良娣有母貞君及兄恭，乃載皇曾孫以付之。

translations.literal: Ji heard Lady Shi's worthy mother had the Chaste Lady and an elder brother Gong; he thereupon carried the imperial great-grandson and handed him over to them.
translations.idiomatic: Ji heard Lady Shi's worthy mother had the Chaste Lady and an elder brother Gong; he thereupon carried the imperial great-grandson and handed him over to them.

sentences.zh: 貞君年老，見孫孤，甚哀之，自養視焉。

translations.literal: The Chaste Lady was old; seeing the grandson orphaned, she deeply pitied him and herself nursed and watched over him.
translations.idiomatic: The Chaste Lady was old; seeing the grandson orphaned, she deeply pitied him and herself nursed and watched over him.

sentences.zh: 後有詔掖庭養視，上屬籍宗正。

translations.literal: Later there was an edict that the Palace Rear Garden should nurse and watch him; the emperor entrusted his registration to the Director of the Imperial Clan.
