translations.idiomatic: Later there was an edict that the Palace Rear Garden should nurse and watch him; the emperor entrusted his registration to the Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 時掖庭令張賀，嘗事戾太子，思顧舊恩，哀曾孫，奉養甚謹，以私錢供給，教書。

translations.literal: At that time Palace Rear Garden Director Zhang He had once served Prince Li; thinking back on old grace, he pitied the great-grandson, supported and nursed him very carefully, supplied him with private money, and taught him books.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Palace Rear Garden Director Zhang He had once served Prince Li; thinking back on old grace, he pitied the great-grandson, supported and nursed him very carefully, supplied him with private money, and taught him books.

sentences.zh: 既壯，賀欲以女孫妻之。

translations.literal: When he was grown, He wished to give his granddaughter in marriage to him.
translations.idiomatic: When he was grown, He wished to give his granddaughter in marriage to him.

sentences.zh: 是時昭帝始冠，長八尺二寸。

translations.literal: At this time Emperor Zhao had just capped his years and was eight feet two inches tall.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Emperor Zhao had just capped his years and was eight feet two inches tall.

sentences.zh: 賀弟安世為右將軍，輔政，聞賀稱譽皇曾孫，欲妻以女，怒曰：「曾孫乃衛太子後也，幸得以庶人衣食縣官足矣，勿復言予女事！

translations.literal: He's younger brother Anshi was Right General assisting government; hearing He praise the imperial great-grandson, he wished to give his daughter in marriage to him and angrily said: "The great-grandson is the heir of the Wei crown prince; it is luck enough that as a commoner he eats and is clothed by the district officials—do not again speak of giving a daughter!
translations.idiomatic: He's younger brother Anshi was Right General assisting government; hearing He praise the imperial great-grandson, he wished to give his daughter in marriage to him and angrily said, "The great-grandson is the heir of the Wei crown prince; it is luck enough that as a commoner he eats and is clothed by the district officials—do not again speak of giving a daughter!

sentences.zh: 」於是賀止。

translations.literal: " Thereupon He stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon He stopped.

sentences.zh: 時暴室嗇夫許廣漢有女，賀乃置酒請廣漢，酒酣，為言：「曾孫體近，下乃關內侯，可妻也。

translations.literal: At that time Wardrobe Provisioner Xu Guanghan had a daughter; He thereupon set out wine and invited Guanghan; when the wine was deep, he spoke for him: "The great-grandson's person is close; below he will be Marquis within the Passes—he can be married.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wardrobe Provisioner Xu Guanghan had a daughter; He thereupon set out wine and invited Guanghan; when the wine was deep, he spoke for him, "The great-grandson's person is close; below he will be Marquis within the Passes—he can be married.

sentences.zh: 」廣漢許諾。

translations.literal: " Guanghan promised.
translations.idiomatic: " Guanghan promised.

sentences.zh: 明日，嫗聞之，怒。

translations.literal: The next day the old woman heard it and was angry.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the old woman heard it and was angry.

sentences.zh: 廣漢重令人為介，遂與曾孫。

translations.literal: Guanghan again had someone act as go-between, and thereupon he was given to the great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Guanghan again had someone act as go-between, and thereupon he was given to the great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 賀以家財聘之。

translations.literal: He used family wealth as betrothal gift.
translations.idiomatic: He used family wealth as betrothal gift.

sentences.zh: 曾孫因依倚廣漢兄弟及祖母家史氏，受《詩》於東海澓中翁，高材好學；

translations.literal: The great-grandson thereby relied on Guanghan's brothers and his grandmother's Shi clan; he received the Odes from Old Man Fu of the Middle in Donghai—talented and fond of learning;
translations.idiomatic: The great-grandson thereby relied on Guanghan's brothers and his grandmother's Shi clan; he received the Odes from Old Man Fu of the Middle in Donghai—talented and fond of learning;

sentences.zh: 然亦喜遊俠，鬥雞走狗，以是俱知-{閭里}-奸邪，吏治得失。

translations.literal: yet he also delighted in roaming knights-errant, cockfighting, and dog-racing—thereby altogether knowing -{閭里}- wickedness and rectitude and officials' governance gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: yet he also delighted in roaming knights-errant, cockfighting, and dog-racing—thereby altogether knowing -{閭里}- wickedness and rectitude and officials' governance gains and losses.

sentences.zh: 數上下諸陵，周遍三輔，嘗困於蓮勺鹵中，尤樂杜、鄠之間，率常在下杜。

translations.literal: He repeatedly went up and down the various mausoleums and circled the Three Metropolises; he once was stranded in the Liaoshao salt marshes; he especially delighted in the region between Du and Hu—he mostly was often at Lower Du.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly went up and down the various mausoleums and circled the Three Metropolises; he once was stranded in the Liaoshao salt marshes; he especially delighted in the region between Du and Hu—he mostly was often at Lower Du.

sentences.zh: 時會朝請，舍長安尚冠-{里}-。

translations.literal: When court audiences were held he lodged in Chang'an at Shangguan -{里}-.
translations.idiomatic: When court audiences were held he lodged in Chang'an at Shangguan -{里}-.

sentences.zh: 及昌邑王廢，霍光與張安世諸大臣議所立，未定。

translations.literal: When the King of Changyi was deposed, Huo Guang with Zhang Anshi and the various great ministers deliberated whom to establish—it was not settled.
translations.idiomatic: When the King of Changyi was deposed, Huo Guang with Zhang Anshi and the various great ministers deliberated whom to establish—it was not settled.

sentences.zh: 丙吉奏記光曰：「將軍事孝武皇帝，受襁褓之屬，任天下之寄。

translations.literal: Bing Ji submitted a note to Guang, saying: "The general served Emperor Wu of Filial Piety, received the entrustment in swaddling clothes, and bore the charge of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Ji submitted a note to Guang, saying, "The general served Emperor Wu of Filial Piety, received the entrustment in swaddling clothes, and bore the charge of all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 孝昭皇帝早崩亡嗣，海內憂懼，欲亟聞嗣主。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhao of Filial Piety early perished without an heir; within the seas there was worry and fear, wishing quickly to hear of a successor lord.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhao of Filial Piety early perished without an heir; within the seas there was worry and fear, wishing quickly to hear of a successor lord.

sentences.zh: 發喪之日，以大誼立後，所立非其人，復以大誼廢之；

translations.literal: On the day mourning was raised, by great principle he established a successor; the one established was not the right person, and again by great principle he deposed him;
translations.idiomatic: On the day mourning was raised, by great principle he established a successor; the one established was not the right person, and again by great principle he deposed him;

sentences.zh: 天下莫不服焉。

translations.literal: all under Heaven none failed to submit to it.
translations.idiomatic: all under Heaven none failed to submit to it.

sentences.zh: 方今社稷、宗廟、群生之命在將軍之壹舉，竊伏聽於眾庶，察其所言諸侯、宗室在列位者，未有所聞於民間也。

translations.literal: Now the altars of soil and grain, the ancestral temples, and the lives of the masses rest on the general's one act; your subject privately bows and listens to the multitude—examining what they say, of the feudal lords and imperial clansmen in ranked positions, nothing has been heard from among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Now the altars of soil and grain, the ancestral temples, and the lives of the masses rest on the general's one act; your subject privately bows and listens to the multitude—examining what they say, of the feudal lords and imperial clansmen in ranked positions, nothing has been heard from among the people.

sentences.zh: 而遺詔所養武帝曾孫名病已在掖庭、外家者，吉前使居郡邸時，見其幼少；

translations.literal: Yet the late emperor's edict–nurtured imperial great-grandson of Emperor Wu named Bingyi, who is in the Palace Rear Garden and at his maternal kin's—when Ji formerly had him dwell at the commandery hostel, he saw him young;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the late emperor's edict–nurtured imperial great-grandson of Emperor Wu named Bingyi, who is in the Palace Rear Garden and at his maternal kin's—when Ji formerly had him dwell at the commandery hostel, he saw him young;

sentences.zh: 至今十八九矣，通經術，有美材，行安而節和。

translations.literal: until now he is eighteen or nineteen; he has mastered the classics, has fine talent, and his conduct is steady and his temperance harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: until now he is eighteen or nineteen; he has mastered the classics, has fine talent, and his conduct is steady and his temperance harmonious.

sentences.zh: 願將軍詳大義，參以蓍龜豈宜，褒顯先使入侍，令天下昭然知之，然後決定大策，天下幸甚！

translations.literal: Your subject wishes the general to examine great principle, consult tortoise and milfoil on what is fitting, honor and display him first and have him enter attendance, let all under Heaven clearly know it, and then decide the great policy—all under Heaven would be greatly fortunate!
translations.idiomatic: Your subject wishes the general to examine great principle, consult tortoise and milfoil on what is fitting, honor and display him first and have him enter attendance, let all under Heaven clearly know it, and then decide the great policy—all under Heaven would be greatly fortunate!

sentences.zh: 」杜延年亦知曾孫德美，勸光、安世立焉。

translations.literal: " Du Yanian also knew the great-grandson's virtue and beauty and urged Guang and Anshi to establish him.
translations.idiomatic: " Du Yanian also knew the great-grandson's virtue and beauty and urged Guang and Anshi to establish him.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，光坐庭中，會丞相以下議定所立，遂復與丞相敞等上奏曰：「孝武皇帝曾孫病已，年十八，師受《詩》、《論語》、《孝經》，躬行節儉，慈仁愛人，可以嗣孝昭皇帝後，奉承祖宗廟，子萬姓。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Guang sat in the courtyard and convened the chancellor and below to settle whom to establish; he thereupon again with Chancellor Chang and others submitted a memorial, saying: "Emperor Wu of Filial Piety's imperial great-grandson Bingyi, age eighteen, has been instructed in the Odes, Analects, and Classic of Filial Piety, personally practices frugality, is kindly and humane, and can succeed after Emperor Zhao of Filial Piety, receive and uphold the ancestral temples, and be lord to the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Guang sat in the courtyard and convened the chancellor and below to settle whom to establish; he thereupon again with Chancellor Chang and others submitted a memorial, saying, "Emperor Wu of Filial Piety's imperial great-grandson Bingyi, age eighteen, has been instructed in the Odes, Analects, and Classic of Filial Piety, personally practices frugality, is kindly and humane, and can succeed after Emperor Zhao of Filial Piety, receive and uphold the ancestral temples, and be lord to the myriad people.

sentences.zh: 臣昧死以聞！

translations.literal: Your subjects risk death to report!
translations.idiomatic: Your subjects risk death to report!

sentences.zh: 」皇太后詔曰：「可。

translations.literal: " The empress dowager edicted: "Approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager edicted, "Approved.

sentences.zh: 」光遣宗正德至曾孫家尚冠-{里}-，洗沐，賜御衣；

translations.literal: " Guang sent Director of the Imperial Clan De to the great-grandson's home at Shangguan -{里}- to bathe and wash him and bestow imperial robes;
translations.idiomatic: " Guang sent Director of the Imperial Clan De to the great-grandson's home at Shangguan -{里}- to bathe and wash him and bestow imperial robes;

sentences.zh: 太僕以軨獵車迎曾孫，就齋宗正府。

translations.literal: the Grand Coachman with a light hunting carriage welcomed the great-grandson, and he fasted at the Director of the Imperial Clan's office.
translations.idiomatic: the Grand Coachman with a light hunting carriage welcomed the great-grandson, and he fasted at the Director of the Imperial Clan's office.

sentences.zh: 庚申，入未央宮，見皇太后，封為陽武侯。

translations.literal: On gengshen he entered Weiyang Palace, saw the empress dowager, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangwu.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen he entered Weiyang Palace, saw the empress dowager, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangwu.

sentences.zh: 已而群臣奏上璽綬，即皇帝位，謁高廟；

translations.literal: Shortly after, the ministers memorialized and presented the seal and ribbon; he took the imperial throne and visited the High Ancestral Temple;
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after, the ministers memorialized and presented the seal and ribbon; he took the imperial throne and visited the High Ancestral Temple;

sentences.zh: 尊皇太后為太皇太后。

translations.literal: he honored the empress dowager as Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: he honored the empress dowager as Grand Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 侍御史嚴延年劾奏「大將軍光擅廢立主，無人臣禮，不道。

translations.literal: Attendant Censor Yan Yannian impeached and memorialized: "Grand General Guang on his own authority deposed and established the lord, lacked minister's rites, and was without the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Censor Yan Yannian impeached and memorialized, "Grand General Guang on his own authority deposed and established the lord, lacked minister's rites, and was without the Way.

sentences.zh: 」奏雖寢，然朝廷肅然敬憚之。

translations.literal: " The memorial though was shelved, yet the court was solemn and in reverent awe of him.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial though was shelved, yet the court was solemn and in reverent awe of him.

translations.literal: ----7 In the ninth month, amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 In the ninth month, there was an amnesty for all under Heaven.

translations.literal: ----8 On wuyin, Cai Yi was made chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: ----8 On wuyin, Cai Yi was appointed chancellor.

translations.literal: ----9 At the beginning, Xu Guanghan's daughter was married to the imperial great-grandson; at one year she bore a son Shi.
translations.idiomatic: ----9 At the beginning, Xu Guanghan's daughter was married to the imperial great-grandson; at one year she bore a son Shi.

sentences.zh: 數月，曾孫立為帝，許氏為倢伃。

translations.literal: Several months later the great-grandson was established as emperor; the Xu clan became Lady of Handsome Fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later the great-grandson was established as emperor; the Xu clan became Lady of Handsome Fairness.

translations.literal: At this time General Huo had a young daughter kin to the empress dowager; the dukes and ministers deliberated on changing and establishing an empress—all inwardly had in mind General Huo's daughter, yet none spoke.
translations.idiomatic: At this time General Huo had a young daughter kin to the empress dowager; the dukes and ministers deliberated on changing and establishing an empress—all inwardly had in mind General Huo's daughter, yet none spoke.

sentences.zh: 上乃詔求微時故劍。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon edicted to seek the old sword from his humble days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon edicted to seek the old sword from his humble days.

sentences.zh: 大臣知指，白立許倢伃為皇后。

translations.literal: The great ministers knew his intent and reported to establish Lady Xu of Handsome Fairness as empress.
translations.idiomatic: The great ministers knew his intent and reported to establish Lady Xu of Handsome Fairness as empress.

sentences.zh: 十一月，壬子，立皇后許氏。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on renzi, Empress Xu was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on renzi, Empress Xu was established.

sentences.zh: 霍光以-{后}-父廣漢刑人，不宜君國；

translations.literal: Huo Guang, because the -{后}-'s father Guanghan was a punished man, thought him unsuitable to lord the state;
translations.idiomatic: Huo Guang, because the -{后}-'s father Guanghan was a punished man, thought him unsuitable to lord the state;

sentences.zh: 歲餘，乃封為昌成君。

translations.literal: after more than a year he was enfeoffed as Lord of Changcheng.
translations.idiomatic: after more than a year he was enfeoffed as Lord of Changcheng.

translations.literal: ----10 The Grand Empress Dowager returned to Changle Palace.
translations.idiomatic: ----10 The Grand Empress Dowager returned to Changle Palace.

sentences.zh: 長樂宮初置屯衛。

translations.literal: Changle Palace for the first time established garrison guards.
translations.idiomatic: Changle Palace for the first time established garrison guards.

sentences.zh: 1春，詔有司論定策安宗廟功。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, an edict ordered the officials to discuss and fix merit for the policy of securing the ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In spring, an edict ordered the officials to discuss and fix merit for the policy of securing the ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 大將軍光益封萬七千戶，與故所食凡二萬戶。

translations.literal: Grand General Guang was additionally enfeoffed with seventeen thousand households; together with what he formerly ate, in all twenty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Guang was additionally enfeoffed with seventeen thousand households; together with what he formerly ate, in all twenty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍富平侯安世以下益封者十人，封侯者五人，賜爵關內侯者八人。

translations.literal: Commandant of Cavalry and Chariots Anshi, Marquis of Fuping, and below—ten persons were additionally enfeoffed; five were enfeoffed as marquises; eight were granted the title Marquis within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of Cavalry and Chariots Anshi, Marquis of Fuping, and below—ten persons were additionally enfeoffed; five were enfeoffed as marquises; eight were granted the title Marquis within the Passes.

sentences.zh: ----2大將軍光稽首歸政，上謙讓不受；

translations.literal: ----2 Grand General Guang bowed his head and returned government; the emperor modestly declined and would not receive it;
translations.idiomatic: ----2 Grand General Guang bowed his head and returned government; the emperor modestly declined and would not receive it;

sentences.zh: 諸事皆先關白光，然後奏御。

translations.literal: all affairs were first brought to Guang's attention, and then memorialized to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: all affairs were first brought to Guang's attention, and then memorialized to the throne.

sentences.zh: 自昭帝時，光子禹及兄孫雲皆為中郎將，雲弟山奉車都尉、侍中、領胡、越兵，光兩女婿為東、西宮衛尉，昆弟、諸婿、外孫皆奉朝請，為諸曹、大夫、騎都尉、給事中，黨親連體，根據於朝廷。

translations.literal: From Emperor Zhao's time, Guang's son Yu and elder brother's grandson Yun were both Commanders of the Palace Guard; Yun's younger brother Shan was Commandant of the Imperial Carriages, Palace Attendant, and led Hu and Yue troops; Guang's two sons-in-law were Eastern and Western Palace Commandants of the Guard; brothers, sons-in-law, and maternal grandsons all attended court audiences as guests, serving as various bureau heads, grandees, Commandants of Cavalry, and Palace Attendants—faction and kin linked as one body, rooted in the court.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Zhao's time, Guang's son Yu and elder brother's grandson Yun were both Commanders of the Palace Guard; Yun's younger brother Shan was Commandant of the Imperial Carriages, Palace Attendant, and led Hu and Yue troops; Guang's two sons-in-law were Eastern and Western Palace Commandants of the Guard; brothers, sons-in-law, and maternal grandsons all attended court audiences as guests, serving as various bureau heads, grandees, Commandants of Cavalry, and Palace Attendants—faction and kin linked as one body, rooted in the court.

sentences.zh: 及昌邑王廢，光權益重，每朝見，上虛己斂容，禮下之已甚。

translations.literal: When the King of Changyi was deposed, Guang's power grew ever heavier; at each court audience the emperor emptied himself and composed his countenance, honoring and lowering himself to him already to excess.
translations.idiomatic: When the King of Changyi was deposed, Guang's power grew ever heavier; at each court audience the emperor emptied himself and composed his countenance, honoring and lowering himself to him already to excess.

sentences.zh: ----3夏，四月，庚午，地震。

translations.literal: ----3 In summer, the fourth month, on gengwu, there was an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In summer, the fourth month, on gengwu, there was an earthquake.

sentences.zh: ----4五月，鳳皇集膠東、千乘。

translations.literal: ----4 In the fifth month, phoenixes gathered at Jiaodong and Qiancheng.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In the fifth month, phoenixes gathered at Jiaodong and Qiancheng.

sentences.zh: 赦天下，勿收田租賦。

translations.literal: Amnesty for all under Heaven; do not collect field rent and tax.
translations.idiomatic: There was an amnesty for all under Heaven; field rent and tax were not collected.

sentences.zh: ----5六月，詔曰：「故皇太子在湖，未有號謚，歲時祠；

translations.literal: ----5 In the sixth month, an edict said: "The former crown prince is at Hu and has no posthumous title or seasonal sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: ----5 In the sixth month, an edict said, "The former crown prince is at Hu and has no posthumous title or seasonal sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 其議謚，置園邑。

translations.literal: discuss his posthumous title and establish a park estate.
translations.idiomatic: discuss his posthumous title and establish a park estate.

sentences.zh: 」有司奏請：「禮，為人後者，為之子也；

translations.literal: " The officials memorialized and requested: "By ritual, one who becomes another's successor is as his son;
translations.idiomatic: " The officials memorialized and requested, "By ritual, one who becomes another's successor is as his son;

sentences.zh: 故降其父母，不得祭，尊祖之義也。

translations.literal: therefore one lowers his parents and may not sacrifice to them—the meaning of honoring ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: therefore one lowers his parents and may not sacrifice to them—the meaning of honoring ancestors.

sentences.zh: 陛下為孝昭帝後，承祖宗之祀，愚以為親謚宜曰悼，母曰-{悼后}-；

translations.literal: Your Majesty succeeds after Emperor Zhao of Filial Piety and receives the ancestral sacrifices; your subjects think the parent's posthumous title should be called Mournful, the mother called -{悼后}-;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty succeeds after Emperor Zhao of Filial Piety and receives the ancestral sacrifices; your subjects think the parent's posthumous title should be called Mournful, the mother called -{悼后}-;

sentences.zh: 故皇太子謚曰戾，史良娣曰戾夫人。

translations.literal: the former crown prince's posthumous title is called Harsh, Lady Shi the worthy is called Lady Harsh.
translations.idiomatic: the former crown prince's posthumous title is called Harsh, Lady Shi the worthy is called Lady Harsh.

sentences.zh: 」皆改葬焉。

translations.literal: " All were reburied.
translations.idiomatic: " All were reburied.

sentences.zh: ----6秋，七月，詔立燕剌王太子建為廣陽王；

translations.literal: ----6 In autumn, the seventh month, an edict established the King of Yan's spur-king crown prince Jian as King of Guangyang;
translations.idiomatic: ----6 In autumn, the seventh month, an edict established the King of Yan's spur-king crown prince Jian as King of Guangyang;

sentences.zh: 立廣陵王胥少子弘為高密王。

translations.literal: it established the King of Guangling Xu's youngest son Hong as King of Gaomi.
translations.idiomatic: it established the King of Guangling Xu's youngest son Hong as King of Gaomi.

sentences.zh: ----7初，上官桀與霍光爭權，光既誅桀，遂遵武帝法度，以刑罰痛繩群下，由是俗吏皆尚嚴酷以為能；

translations.literal: ----7 At the beginning, Shangguan Jie contended for power with Huo Guang; after Guang had executed Jie, he thereupon followed Emperor Wu's standards, using punishments to tightly bind the masses below—thereby vulgar officials all prized severity and cruelty as ability;
translations.idiomatic: ----7 At the beginning, Shangguan Jie contended for power with Huo Guang; after Guang had executed Jie, he thereupon followed Emperor Wu's standards, using punishments to tightly bind the masses below—thereby vulgar officials all prized severity and cruelty as ability;

sentences.zh: 而河南太守丞淮陽黃霸獨用寬和為名。

translations.literal: yet Assistant Governor Huang Ba of Huaiyang in Henan alone used leniency and harmony as his reputation.
translations.idiomatic: yet Assistant Governor Huang Ba of Huaiyang in Henan alone used leniency and harmony as his reputation.

sentences.zh: 上在民間時，知百姓苦吏急也，聞霸持法平，乃召以為廷尉正；

translations.literal: When the emperor was among the people he knew the common people suffered from officials' harshness; hearing Ba held the law evenly, he thereupon summoned him and made him Corrector of the Commandant of Justice;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was among the people he knew the common people suffered from officials' harshness; hearing Ba held the law evenly, he thereupon summoned him and made him Corrector of the Commandant of Justice;

sentences.zh: 數決疑獄，庭中稱平。

translations.literal: he repeatedly decided doubtful cases, and within the court they called him even.
translations.idiomatic: he repeatedly decided doubtful cases, and within the court they called him even.

sentences.zh: 1春，大司農田延年有罪自殺。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, Grand Minister of Agriculture Tian Yannian, guilty of a crime, killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In spring, Grand Minister of Agriculture Tian Yannian, guilty of a crime, killed himself.

sentences.zh: 昭帝之喪，大司農僦民車，延年詐增僦直，盜取錢三千萬，為怨家所告。

translations.literal: At Emperor Zhao's mourning, the Grand Minister of Agriculture hired the people's carts; Yannian falsely increased the hire price and stole thirty million cash; he was reported by an enemy family.
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Zhao's mourning, the Grand Minister of Agriculture hired the people's carts; Yannian falsely increased the hire price and stole thirty million cash; he was reported by an enemy family.

sentences.zh: 霍將軍召問延年，欲為道地。

translations.literal: The Grand General summoned and questioned Yannian, wishing to show him a way out.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Huo summoned and questioned Yannian, wishing to find him grounds for leniency.

sentences.zh: 延年抵曰：「無有是事！

translations.literal: Yannian resisted and said: "There is no such thing!
translations.idiomatic: Yannian pushed back and said, "There is no such thing!

sentences.zh: 」光曰：「即無事，當窮竟！

translations.literal: " Guang said: "Even if there is nothing, it must be thoroughly investigated!
translations.idiomatic: " Guang said, "Even if there is nothing to it, it must be investigated to the end!

sentences.zh: 」御史大夫田廣明謂太僕杜延年曰：「《春秋》之義，以功覆過。

translations.literal: " The Censor-in-Chief Tian Guangming said to Grand Master of Husbandry Du Yannian: "The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that merit covers offense.
translations.idiomatic: " Censor-in-Chief Tian Guangming said to Grand Master of Husbandry Du Yannian, "The Spring and Autumn principle is that merit may cover offense.

sentences.zh: 當廢昌邑王時，非田子賓之言，大事不成。

translations.literal: When deposing the King of Changyi, without Tian Zibin's words the great affair would not have succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When deposing the King of Changyi, without Tian Zibin's counsel the great affair would not have succeeded.

sentences.zh: 今縣官出三千萬自乞之，何哉？

translations.literal: Now the official treasury puts out thirty million to beg for himself—what is this?
translations.idiomatic: Now the government is putting out thirty million to plead on his behalf—what is this?

sentences.zh: 願以愚言白大將軍。

translations.literal: I wish to present my foolish words to inform the Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to present my humble counsel to the Grand General.

sentences.zh: 」延年言之大將軍，大將軍曰：「誠然，實勇士也！

translations.literal: " Yannian reported it to the Grand General; the Grand General said: "It is truly so—he is indeed a brave warrior!
translations.idiomatic: " Yannian reported this to the Grand General, who said, "It is true—he is indeed a brave warrior!

sentences.zh: 當發大議時，震動朝廷，」光因舉手自撫心曰：「使我至今病悸。

translations.literal: When the great debate was launched, it shook the court," Guang thereupon raised his hand and stroked his heart, saying: "It makes my heart palpitate with illness even now.
translations.idiomatic: When that great debate was launched, it shook the court," Guang raised his hand to his heart and said, "It still makes my heart race with fear.

sentences.zh: 謝田大夫曉大司農，通往就獄，得公議之。

translations.literal: Thank Censor Tian; inform the Grand Minister of Agriculture; enable him to proceed to prison and obtain the court's collective deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Thank Censor Tian; inform the Grand Minister of Agriculture; let him go to prison and obtain a collective court judgment.

sentences.zh: 」田大夫使人語延年。

translations.literal: " The Censor sent someone to speak to Yannian.
translations.idiomatic: " The Censor sent someone to speak to Yannian.

sentences.zh: 延年曰：「幸縣官寬我耳，何面目入牢獄，使眾人指笑我，卒徒唾吾背乎？

translations.literal: Yannian said: "Fortunately the official treasury will be lenient with me—what face have I to enter prison, let the multitude point and laugh at me, and convicts and soldiers spit on my back?
translations.idiomatic: Yannian said, "Fortunately the government will be lenient with me—what face have I to enter prison, let everyone point and laugh at me, and convicts spit on my back?

sentences.zh: 」即閉閣獨居齋舍，偏袒，持刀東西步。

translations.literal: " He immediately shut the door, lived alone in his study quarters, bared one shoulder, and paced east and west with a knife in hand.
translations.idiomatic: " He shut his door, lived alone in his study, bared one shoulder, and paced east and west with a knife in hand.

sentences.zh: 數日，使者召延年詣廷尉。

translations.literal: Several days later, an envoy summoned Yannian to the Director of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later, an envoy summoned Yannian to the Director of Justice.

sentences.zh: 聞鼓聲，自刎死。

translations.literal: Hearing the drum sound, he cut his own throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the drum, he cut his own throat and died.

sentences.zh: ----2夏，五月，詔曰：「孝武皇帝躬仁誼，勵威武，功德茂盛，而廟樂未稱，聯甚悼焉。

translations.literal: ----2 In summer, the fifth month, an edict said: "Emperor Xiao Wu personally practiced benevolence and righteousness, encouraged martial prowess, and his merit and virtue were luxuriant, yet the temple music does not match him—We are deeply grieved.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In summer, the fifth month, an edict said, "Emperor Xiao Wu personally practiced benevolence and righteousness, encouraged martial prowess, and his merit and virtue were abundant, yet his temple music is unworthy—We are deeply grieved.

sentences.zh: 其與列侯、二千石、博士議。

translations.literal: Let him deliberate with the ranked marquises, the two-thousand-bushel officials, and the erudites.
translations.idiomatic: Let him deliberate with the marquises, two-thousand-bushel officials, and erudites.

sentences.zh: 」於是群臣大議庭中，皆曰：「宜如詔書。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the ministers greatly debated in the court, all saying: "It should be as the edict states.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the ministers debated at length in court, all saying, "It should be as the edict states.

sentences.zh: 」長信少府夏侯勝獨曰：「武帝雖有攘四夷、廣土境之功，然多殺士眾，竭民財力，奢泰無度，天下虛耗，百姓流離，物故者半，蝗蟲大起，赤地數千里，或人民相食，畜積至今未復；

translations.literal: " Director of Changxin Household Xiahou Sheng alone said: "Although Emperor Wu had the achievement of driving off the four barbarians and expanding the territory, yet he killed many soldiers and masses, exhausted the people's wealth and strength, was extravagant beyond measure—the realm was drained empty, the people were displaced, half died, locusts arose greatly, thousands of li of bare red earth, sometimes people ate one another, and stores have not recovered to this day;
translations.idiomatic: " Director of Changxin Household Xiahou Sheng alone said, "Although Emperor Wu had the achievement of driving off the four barbarians and expanding the borders, he killed many soldiers and civilians, exhausted the people's wealth, was extravagant beyond measure—the realm was drained, the people displaced, half perished, locusts swarmed, thousands of li lay bare, people sometimes ate one another, and stores have not recovered to this day;

sentences.zh: 無德澤於民，不宜為立廟樂。

translations.literal: he had no benevolent favor toward the people and is not fit to have temple music established.
translations.idiomatic: he bestowed no benevolent favor on the people and is not fit to have temple music established.

sentences.zh: 」公卿共難勝曰：「此詔書也。

translations.literal: " The high ministers together challenged Sheng, saying: "This is an imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: " The high ministers together challenged Sheng, saying, "This is an imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 」勝曰：「詔書不可用也。

translations.literal: " Sheng said: "The edict cannot be used.
translations.idiomatic: " Sheng said, "The edict cannot be followed.

sentences.zh: 人臣之誼，宜直言正論，非苟阿意順指。

translations.literal: The duty of a minister is to speak straight and argue correctly—not to fawn to please and follow the finger.
translations.idiomatic: A minister's duty is to speak frankly and argue rightly—not to fawn and follow every whim.

sentences.zh: 議已出口，雖死不悔！

translations.literal: The discussion has already left my mouth—even if I die I will not regret it!
translations.idiomatic: What I have said is already spoken—even if I die I will not regret it!

sentences.zh: 」於是丞相、御史劾奏勝非議詔書，毀先帝，不道；

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Chancellor and Censor impeached Sheng for criticizing the edict, slandering the former emperor, and impiety;
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the chancellor and censor impeached Sheng for criticizing the edict, slandering the former emperor, and impiety;

sentences.zh: 及丞相長史黃霸阿縱勝，不舉劾；

translations.literal: and the Chancellor's Chief Clerk Huang Ba indulged and indulged Sheng, failing to impeach;
translations.idiomatic: and the chancellor's chief clerk Huang Ba indulged Sheng and failed to impeach him;

sentences.zh: 俱下獄。

translations.literal: both were sent to prison.
translations.idiomatic: both were imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 有司遂請尊孝武帝廟為世宗廟，奏《盛德》、《文始五行》之舞。

translations.literal: The responsible offices thereupon requested to honor Emperor Xiao Wu's temple as the Shizong Temple and perform the dances "Abundant Virtue" and "Wen Shi Five Elements."
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices requested honoring Emperor Xiao Wu's temple as the Shizong Temple and performing the dances "Abundant Virtue" and "Wen Shi Five Elements."

sentences.zh: 武帝巡狩所幸郡國皆立廟，如高祖、太宗焉。

translations.literal: In every commandery and state where Emperor Wu toured and favored, temples were established, as with Gaozu and Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: In every commandery and state Emperor Wu had favored on his tours, temples were established, as with Gaozu and Taizong.

sentences.zh: 夏侯勝、黃霸既久繫，霸欲從勝受《尚書》，勝辭以罪死。

translations.literal: Xiahou Sheng and Huang Ba, having long been imprisoned, Ba wished to receive the Documents from Sheng; Sheng declined on the grounds that he would die for his offense.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Sheng and Huang Ba, long imprisoned, wished to study the Documents with Sheng; Sheng declined, saying he would die for his offense.

sentences.zh: 霸曰：「朝聞道，夕死可矣。

translations.literal: Ba said: "If one hears the Way in the morning, one may die in the evening.
translations.idiomatic: Ba said, "If one hears the Way in the morning, one may die in the evening.

sentences.zh: 」勝賢其言，遂授之。

translations.literal: " Sheng esteemed his words and thereupon taught him.
translations.idiomatic: " Sheng admired his words and thereupon taught him.

sentences.zh: 繫再更冬，講論不怠。

translations.literal: Imprisoned through two more winters, they lectured and discussed without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: Imprisoned through two more winters, they lectured without slackening.

sentences.zh: ----3初，烏孫公主死，漢復以楚王戊之孫解憂為公主，妻岑娶。

translations.literal: ----3 Initially the Wusun princess died; Han again made Jieyou, granddaughter of King Wu of Chu, princess and married her to Cenju.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 Initially the Wusun princess died; Han again made Jieyou, granddaughter of King Wu of Chu, a princess and married her to Cenju.

sentences.zh: 岑娶胡婦子泥靡尚小，岑娶且死，以國與季父大祿子翁歸靡，曰：「泥靡大，以國歸之。

translations.literal: Cenju's son by a Hu woman, Nimi, was still young; as Cenju was about to die, he gave the state to his younger father's son, the Grand Captain's son Wengguimi, saying: "When Nimi is grown, return the state to him.
translations.idiomatic: Cenju's son by a Hu woman, Nimi, was still young; as Cenju was dying, he gave the state to his uncle's son Wengguimi, saying, "When Nimi is grown, return the state to him.

sentences.zh: 」翁歸靡既立，號肥王，復尚楚主，生三男、兩女。

translations.literal: " Wengguimi, once installed, was titled the Fat King; he again married the Chu princess and begot three sons and two daughters.
translations.idiomatic: " Once installed, Wengguimi was titled the Fat King; he again married the Chu princess and had three sons and two daughters.

sentences.zh: 長男曰元貴靡，次曰萬年，次曰大樂。

translations.literal: The eldest son was called Yuanguimi, the second Wannian, the third Dale.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son was Yuanguimi, the second Wannian, the third Dale.

sentences.zh: 昭帝時，公主上書言：「匈奴與車師共侵烏孫，唯天子幸救之。

translations.literal: In Emperor Zhao's time the princess memorialized, saying: "The Xiongnu and Cheshi together invade Wusun—only the Son of Heaven may deign to save us.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Zhao's time the princess memorialized, "The Xiongnu and Cheshi together invade Wusun—only the Son of Heaven can save us.

translations.literal: " Han raised soldiers and horses and debated attacking the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: " Han raised troops and horses and debated attacking the Xiongnu.

translations.literal: It happened Emperor Zhao died; the emperor dispatched Palace Counselor Chang Hui as envoy to Wusun.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhao died; the emperor dispatched Palace Counselor Chang Hui as envoy to Wusun.

sentences.zh: 烏孫公主及昆彌皆遣使上書，言：「匈奴復連發大兵，侵擊烏孫。

translations.literal: The Wusun princess and the kunmi both sent envoys memorializing, saying: "The Xiongnu again repeatedly dispatch great armies to invade and strike Wusun.
translations.idiomatic: The Wusun princess and the kunmi both memorialized, "The Xiongnu again repeatedly dispatch great armies to invade Wusun.

sentences.zh: 使使謂烏孫，『趣持公主來！

translations.literal: They send envoys telling Wusun, 'Hurry and bring the princess here!
translations.idiomatic: They send envoys telling Wusun, 'Hurry and bring the princess here!

sentences.zh: 』欲隔絕漢。

translations.literal: ' wishing to cut off Han.
translations.idiomatic: ' intending to sever ties with Han.

translations.literal: The kunmi wishes to dispatch the state's elite troops, fifty thousand horsemen, and strike the Xiongnu with full force.
translations.idiomatic: The kunmi wishes to dispatch fifty thousand elite horsemen and strike the Xiongnu with full force.

sentences.zh: 唯天子出兵以救公主、昆彌！

translations.literal: Only the Son of Heaven must dispatch troops to save the princess and the kunmi!
translations.idiomatic: Only the Son of Heaven can dispatch troops to save the princess and the kunmi!

sentences.zh: 」先是匈奴數侵漢邊，漢亦欲討之。

translations.literal: " Earlier the Xiongnu had repeatedly invaded Han's borders, and Han also wished to chastise them.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier the Xiongnu had repeatedly invaded Han's borders, and Han also wished to chastise them.

translations.literal: In autumn great forces were raised; the Censor-in-Chief Tian Guangming was made General of Qilian, with more than forty thousand horsemen, out from Xihe;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn great forces were raised; Censor-in-Chief Tian Guangming was made General of Qilian with more than forty thousand horsemen, marching out from Xihe;

sentences.zh: 度遼將軍范明友三萬餘騎，出張掖；

translations.literal: General Crossing the Liao Fan Mingyou with more than thirty thousand horsemen, out from Zhangye;
translations.idiomatic: General Crossing the Liao Fan Mingyou with more than thirty thousand horsemen, out from Zhangye;

sentences.zh: 前將軍韓增三萬餘騎，出雲中；

translations.literal: Forward General Han Zeng with more than thirty thousand horsemen, out from Yunzhong;
translations.idiomatic: Forward General Han Zeng with more than thirty thousand horsemen, out from Yunzhong;

sentences.zh: 後將軍趙充國為蒲類將軍，三萬餘騎，出酒泉；

translations.literal: Rear General Zhao Chongguo as General of Pu Lei with more than thirty thousand horsemen, out from Jiuquan;
translations.idiomatic: Rear General Zhao Chongguo as General of Pu Lei with more than thirty thousand horsemen, out from Jiuquan;

sentences.zh: 雲中太守田順為虎牙將軍，三萬餘騎，出五原；

translations.literal: Governor of Yunzhong Tian Shun as General of Tiger's Teeth with more than thirty thousand horsemen, out from Wuyuan;
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Yunzhong Tian Shun as General of Tiger's Teeth with more than thirty thousand horsemen, out from Wuyuan;

sentences.zh: 期以出塞各二千餘里。

translations.literal: they were scheduled to go beyond the passes each more than two thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: they were to go beyond the passes each more than two thousand li.

sentences.zh: 以常惠為校尉，持節護烏孫兵共擊匈奴。

translations.literal: Chang Hui was made colonel, bearing credentials to oversee Wusun troops jointly striking the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Hui was made colonel, bearing credentials to oversee Wusun troops in a joint attack on the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，癸亥，恭哀許皇后崩。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the first month, on guihai, the Respectful and Lamented Empress Xu died.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In spring, the first month, on guihai, the Respectful and Lamented Empress Xu died.

sentences.zh: 時霍光夫人顯欲貴其小女成君，道無從。

translations.literal: At this time Huo Guang's wife Xian wished to exalt her younger daughter Chengjun but found no way.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Huo Guang's wife Xian wished to exalt her younger daughter Chengjun but found no way to do so.

sentences.zh: 會-{許后}-當娠，病，女醫-{淳于衍}-者，霍氏所愛，嘗入宮侍皇后疾。

translations.literal: It happened -{許后}- was about to give birth and was ill; the woman physician -{淳于衍}-, whom the Huo clan favored, had once entered the palace to attend the empress's illness.
translations.idiomatic: It happened -{許后}- was about to give birth and was ill; the woman physician -{淳于衍}-, favored by the Huo clan, had once entered the palace to attend the empress's illness.

sentences.zh: 衍夫賞為掖庭戶衛，謂衍：「可過辭霍夫人，行為我求安池監。

translations.literal: Yan's husband Shang was a Household Guard of the Palace Apartments and said to Yan: "You may go and speak to Lady Huo; on the way seek for me the post of Overseer of Anchi.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's husband Shang was a Household Guard of the Palace Apartments and told Yan, "You may visit Lady Huo; on the way ask for me the post of Overseer of Anchi.

sentences.zh: 」衍如言報顯，顯因生心，辟左右，謂衍曰：「少夫幸報我以事，我亦欲報少夫，可乎？

translations.literal: " Yan reported as told to Xian; Xian thereupon conceived a plan, dismissed those at hand, and said to Yan: "Young lady, if you will report something for me, I also wish to repay the young lady—may I?
translations.idiomatic: " Yan reported as told to Xian; Xian conceived a plan, dismissed attendants, and said to Yan, "Young lady, if you will do something for me, I also wish to repay you—will you?

sentences.zh: 」衍曰：「夫人所言，何等不可者！

translations.literal: " Yan said: "Whatever the lady says—what could not be done!
translations.idiomatic: " Yan said, "Whatever my lady says—what could not be done!

sentences.zh: 」顯曰：「將軍素愛小女成君，欲奇貴之，願以累少夫。

translations.literal: " Xian said: "The General has long loved my younger daughter Chengjun and wishes to exalt her extraordinarily; I wish to entrust this to the young lady.
translations.idiomatic: " Xian said, "The General has long loved my younger daughter Chengjun and wishes to exalt her extraordinarily; I wish to entrust this to you.

sentences.zh: 」衍曰：「何謂邪？

translations.literal: " Yan said: "What does this mean?
translations.idiomatic: " Yan said, "What do you mean?

sentences.zh: 」顯曰：「婦人免乳，大故，十死一生。

translations.literal: " Xian said: "When a woman completes childbirth, it is a great matter—nine deaths to one life.
translations.idiomatic: " Xian said, "Childbirth is a grave matter—nine deaths to one life.

sentences.zh: 今皇后當免身，可因投毒藥去也，成君即為皇后矣。

translations.literal: Now the empress is about to complete childbirth; you may take the opportunity to administer poison and remove her—Chengjun will then be empress.
translations.idiomatic: Now the empress is about to give birth; you may take the opportunity to poison her—Chengjun will then be empress.

sentences.zh: 如蒙力，事成，富貴與少夫共之。

translations.literal: If you grant your strength and the affair succeeds, wealth and honor will be shared with the young lady.
translations.idiomatic: If you lend your strength and it succeeds, wealth and honor will be shared with you.

sentences.zh: 」衍曰：「藥雜治，常先嘗，安可？

translations.literal: " Yan said: "Medicines are mixed and treated—the physician always tastes them first; how could it be done?
translations.idiomatic: " Yan said, "Medicines are compounded and the physician always tastes them first—how could it be done?

sentences.zh: 」顯曰：「在少夫為之耳。

translations.literal: " Xian said: "It lies with the young lady to do it.
translations.idiomatic: " Xian said, "That is for you to do.

sentences.zh: 將軍領天下，誰敢言者！

translations.literal: The General commands all under Heaven—who would dare speak!
translations.idiomatic: The General commands the realm—who would dare speak!

sentences.zh: 緩急相護，但恐少夫無意耳。

translations.literal: In urgency and ease we protect one another—I only fear the young lady has no intent.
translations.idiomatic: In urgency and ease we protect one another—I only fear you lack the will.

sentences.zh: 」衍良久曰：「願盡力！

translations.literal: " After a long while Yan said: "I am willing to exert all my strength!
translations.idiomatic: " After a long while Yan said, "I will do all I can!

sentences.zh: 」即搗附子，賫入長定宮。

translations.literal: " She immediately pounded aconite and carried it into Changding Palace.
translations.idiomatic: " She pounded aconite and carried it into Changding Palace.

sentences.zh: 皇后免身後，衍取附子併合太醫大丸以飲皇后，有頃，曰：「我頭岑岑也，藥中得無有毒？

translations.literal: After the empress completed childbirth, Yan took the aconite, mixed it into the Grand Physician's large pill, and had the empress drink it; after a moment she said: "My head is dizzy—is there perhaps poison in the medicine?
translations.idiomatic: After the empress gave birth, Yan mixed aconite into the Grand Physician's large pill and had her drink it; presently she said, "My head is swimming—could there be poison in the medicine?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「無有。

translations.literal: " The reply was: "There is none.
translations.idiomatic: " The reply was, "There is none.

sentences.zh: 」遂加煩懣，崩。

translations.literal: " She thereupon grew more distressed and vexed and died.
translations.idiomatic: " She grew more distressed and died.

sentences.zh: 衍出，過見顯，相勞問，亦未敢重謝衍。

translations.literal: Yan went out, passed and saw Xian, exchanged greetings, yet did not dare heavily thank Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan went out, saw Xian on the way, exchanged greetings, yet did not dare thank her effusively.

sentences.zh: 後人有上書告諸醫侍疾無狀者，皆收繫詔獄，劾不道。

translations.literal: Later someone memorialized accusing the physicians who attended the illness of misconduct; all were arrested and imprisoned in the edict prison, impeached for impiety.
translations.idiomatic: Later someone memorialized accusing the attending physicians of misconduct; all were arrested in the edict prison and impeached for impiety.

sentences.zh: 顯恐急，即以狀具語光，因曰：「既失計為之，無令吏急衍！

translations.literal: Xian, fearful and urgent, fully told Guang the circumstances, saying: "Having erred in doing this, do not let the officials press Yan!
translations.idiomatic: Xian, in fear, fully told Guang the circumstances and said, "Having erred in this, do not let the officials press Yan!

sentences.zh: 」光大驚，欲自發舉，不忍，猶與。

translations.literal: " Guang was greatly shocked, wished to report it himself, could not bear to, and still hesitated.
translations.idiomatic: " Guang was greatly shocked, wished to report it himself but could not bear to, and still wavered.

sentences.zh: 會奏上，光署衍勿論。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Guang endorsed that Yan not be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Guang endorsed that Yan not be prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 顯因勸光內其女入宮。

translations.literal: Xian thereupon urged Guang to bring her daughter into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Xian urged Guang to bring her daughter into the palace.

sentences.zh: ----2戊辰，五將軍發長安。

translations.literal: ----2 On wuchen the five generals set out from Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 On wuchen the five generals set out from Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 匈奴聞漢兵大出，老弱奔走，驅畜產遠遁逃，是以五將少所得。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu heard Han troops were coming out in force; the old and weak fled in haste, driving livestock far off in escape—thus the five generals gained little.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu heard Han troops were coming out in force; the old and weak fled, driving livestock far off—thus the five generals gained little.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，軍罷。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, the armies were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, the armies were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 度遼將軍出塞千二百餘里，至蒲離候水，斬首、捕虜七百餘級；

translations.literal: General Crossing the Liao went beyond the passes more than twelve hundred li, reached the Puli Marquis's Water, and cut heads and captured prisoners more than seven hundred;
translations.idiomatic: General Crossing the Liao went beyond the passes more than twelve hundred li to Puli Marquis's Water and cut more than seven hundred heads and captives;

sentences.zh: 前將軍出塞千二百餘里，至烏員，斬首、捕虜百餘級；

translations.literal: the Forward General went beyond the passes more than twelve hundred li, reached Wuyuan, and cut heads and captured prisoners more than one hundred;
translations.idiomatic: the Forward General went more than twelve hundred li beyond the passes to Wuyuan and cut more than one hundred heads and captives;

sentences.zh: 蒲類將軍出塞千八百餘里，西至候山，斬首、捕虜，得單于使者蒲陰王以下三百餘級。

translations.literal: the General of Pu Lei went beyond the passes more than eighteen hundred li, west to Hou Mountain, cut heads and captured prisoners, obtaining the Chanyu's envoy Pu Yin Wang and below—more than three hundred;
translations.idiomatic: the General of Pu Lei went more than eighteen hundred li beyond the passes west to Hou Mountain, cut heads and captives, and took the chanyu's envoy Pu Yin Wang and others—more than three hundred;

sentences.zh: 聞虜已引去，皆不至期還。

translations.literal: Hearing the barbarians had already withdrawn, all failed to return by the appointed date.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the enemy had withdrawn, all failed to return by the appointed date.

sentences.zh: 天子薄其過，寬而不罪。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven regarded their offenses lightly and was lenient without punishing them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor regarded their offenses lightly and did not punish them.

sentences.zh: 祁連將軍出塞千六百里，至雞秩山，斬首、捕虜十九級。

translations.literal: General of Qilian went beyond the passes sixteen hundred li, reached Jizhi Mountain, and cut heads and captured prisoners nineteen.
translations.idiomatic: General of Qilian went sixteen hundred li beyond the passes to Jizhi Mountain and cut nineteen heads and captives.

sentences.zh: 逢漢使匈奴還者冉弘等，言雞秩山西有虜眾，祁連即戒弘，使言無虜，欲還兵。

translations.literal: He met Han envoys returning from the Xiongnu, Ran Hong and others, who said west of Jizhi Mountain there were barbarian masses; Qilian immediately warned Hong to say there were no barbarians, wishing to withdraw the army.
translations.idiomatic: He met Han envoys returning from the Xiongnu, Ran Hong and others, who said there were enemy forces west of Jizhi Mountain; Qilian warned Hong to say there were none, wishing to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 御史屬公孫益壽諫，以為主可。

translations.literal: Secretary of the Censorate Gongsun Yishou remonstrated, thinking the commander could do it.
translations.idiomatic: Secretary of the Censorate Gongsun Yishou remonstrated that the commander should advance.

sentences.zh: 祁連不聽，遂引兵還。

translations.literal: Qilian did not listen and thereupon withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Qilian did not listen and withdrew the army.

sentences.zh: 虎牙將軍出塞八百餘里，至丹餘吾水上，即止兵不進，斬首、捕虜千九百餘級，引兵還。

translations.literal: General of Tiger's Teeth went beyond the passes more than eight hundred li, reached the Dan Yuyu River, thereupon halted the army and did not advance, cut heads and captured prisoners more than nineteen hundred, and withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: General of Tiger's Teeth went more than eight hundred li beyond the passes to the Dan Yuyu River, halted without advancing, cut more than nineteen hundred heads and captives, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 上以虎牙將軍不至期，詐增鹵獲，而祁連知虜在前，逗遛不進，皆下吏，自殺。

translations.literal: The emperor, because General of Tiger's Teeth failed to arrive by the date and falsely inflated captive gains, and Qilian knew the barbarians were ahead yet hesitated and did not advance, sent both to the officials; they committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, because General of Tiger's Teeth failed to arrive on time and falsely inflated captures, and Qilian knew the enemy was ahead yet hesitated and did not advance, sent both to the officials; they committed suicide.

sentences.zh: 擢公孫益壽為侍御史。

translations.literal: Gongsun Yishou was promoted to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Yishou was promoted to Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 烏孫昆彌自將五萬騎與校尉常惠從西方入，至右谷蠡王庭，獲單于父行及嫂、居次、名王、犁汙都尉、千長、騎將以下四萬級，馬、牛、羊、驢、橐佗七十餘萬頭。

translations.literal: The Wusun kunmi personally led fifty thousand horsemen with Colonel Chang Hui entering from the west to the Right Guli King's court, obtaining the chanyu's father's generation and elder sister-in-law, younger sisters, named kings, Liyu colonels, thousand-chiefs, cavalry generals and below—forty thousand in rank, and horses, cattle, sheep, donkeys, and camels more than seven hundred thousand head.
translations.idiomatic: The Wusun kunmi personally led fifty thousand horsemen with Colonel Chang Hui, entering from the west to the Right Guli King's court, capturing the chanyu's father's generation, sisters-in-law, younger sisters, named kings, Liyu colonels, thousand-chiefs, cavalry generals and below—forty thousand in rank—and more than seven hundred thousand horses, cattle, sheep, donkeys, and camels.

sentences.zh: 烏孫皆自取所虜獲。

translations.literal: The Wusun all took for themselves what they had captured.
translations.idiomatic: The Wusun kept all they had captured.

sentences.zh: 上以五將皆無功，獨惠奉使克獲，封惠為長羅侯。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the five generals all had no achievement while Hui alone on his mission succeeded in capture, enfeoffed Hui as Marquis of Changluo.
translations.idiomatic: Because the five generals all achieved nothing while Hui alone on his mission succeeded, the emperor enfeoffed Hui as Marquis of Changluo.

sentences.zh: 然匈奴民眾傷而去者及畜產遠移死亡，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Yet the Xiongnu's people wounded and departed and livestock moved far off and died were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xiongnu wounded and displaced people and livestock moved far off and died in numbers beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 於是匈奴遂衰耗，怨烏孫。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Xiongnu declined and were depleted and resented Wusun.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Xiongnu declined and resented Wusun.

sentences.zh: 上復遣常惠持金幣還賜烏孫貴人有功者。

translations.literal: The emperor again dispatched Chang Hui bearing gold and coins to return and bestow on Wusun nobles who had merit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again dispatched Chang Hui with gold and coins to reward meritorious Wusun nobles.

sentences.zh: 惠因奏請龜茲國嘗殺校尉賴丹，未伏誅，請便道擊之。

translations.literal: Hui thereupon memorialized requesting that Kucha had once killed Colonel Lai Dan and had not submitted to execution, and asked to strike them by a convenient route.
translations.idiomatic: Hui thereupon memorialized that Kucha had once killed Colonel Lai Dan without having submitted to punishment, and asked to strike them by a convenient route.

sentences.zh: 帝不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 大將軍霍光風惠以便宜從事。

translations.literal: Grand General Huo Guang hinted to Hui that he might act as expedience required.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Huo Guang hinted to Hui that he might act at his discretion.

sentences.zh: 惠與吏士五百人俱至烏孫，還，過，發西國兵二萬人，令副使發龜茲東國二萬人，烏孫兵七千人，從三面攻龜茲。

translations.literal: Hui, with five hundred clerks and soldiers, together reached Wusun; on the return, passing through, he raised twenty thousand troops of the western states, ordered the deputy envoy to raise twenty thousand of Kucha's eastern states, and seven thousand Wusun troops, and attacked Kucha from three sides.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, with five hundred clerks and soldiers, reached Wusun; on the return march he raised twenty thousand troops of the western states, had the deputy envoy raise twenty thousand from Kucha's eastern dependencies and seven thousand Wusun troops, and attacked Kucha from three sides.

sentences.zh: 兵未合，先遣人責其王以前殺漢使狀。

translations.literal: Before the armies joined, he first sent someone to reproach the king for the earlier killing of Han envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Before the armies converged, he first sent someone to reproach the king for having killed Han envoys.

sentences.zh: 王謝曰：「乃我先王時為貴人姑翼所誤耳，我無罪。

translations.literal: The king apologized, saying: "It was only in my former king's time that the noble Gu Yi misled us—I am without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The king apologized, saying, "It was only in my former king's time that the noble Gu Yi misled us—I am guiltless.

sentences.zh: 」惠曰：「即如此，縛姑翼來，吾置王。

translations.literal: " Hui said: "If it is so, bind Gu Yi and bring him—I will install you as king.
translations.idiomatic: " Hui said, "If so, bind Gu Yi and bring him—I will install you as king.

sentences.zh: 」王執姑翼詣惠，惠斬之而還。

translations.literal: " The king seized Gu Yi and presented him to Hui; Hui beheaded him and returned.
translations.idiomatic: " The king seized Gu Yi and presented him to Hui; Hui beheaded him and returned.

translations.literal: ----3 Great drought.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 There was a great drought.

sentences.zh: ----4六月，己丑，陽平節侯蔡義薨。

translations.literal: ----4 In the sixth month, on jichou, Marquis Jie of Yangping Cai Yi died.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In the sixth month, on jichou, Marquis Jie of Yangping Cai Yi died.

sentences.zh: ----5甲辰，長信少府韋賢為丞相。

translations.literal: ----5 On jiachen, Director of Changxin Household Wei Xian became Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 On jiachen, Director of Changxin Household Wei Xian became chancellor.

sentences.zh: ----6大司農魏相為御史大夫。

translations.literal: ----6 Grand Minister of Agriculture Wei Xiang became Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 Grand Minister of Agriculture Wei Xiang became censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: ----7冬，匈奴單于自將數萬騎擊烏孫，頗得老弱。

translations.literal: ----7 In winter the Xiongnu chanyu personally led tens of thousands of horsemen to strike Wusun and took many of the old and weak.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 In winter the Xiongnu chanyu personally led tens of thousands of horsemen against Wusun and captured many of the old and weak.

sentences.zh: 欲還，會天大雨雪，一日深丈餘，人民、畜產凍死，還者不能什一。

translations.literal: Wishing to return, they encountered heaven's great rain and snow; in one day it was more than a zhang deep; people and livestock froze to death, and of those returning not one in ten.
translations.idiomatic: As they wished to return, heavy rain and snow fell; in one day the snow was more than a zhang deep; people and livestock froze to death, and fewer than one in ten of those who set out returned.

sentences.zh: 於是丁令乘弱攻其北，烏桓入其東，烏孫擊其西，凡三國所殺數萬級，馬數萬匹，牛羊甚眾；

translations.literal: Thereupon the Dingling, taking advantage of weakness, struck their north; the Wuhuan entered their east; Wusun struck their west—in all the three states killed tens of thousands, tens of thousands of horses, and very many cattle and sheep;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Dingling, seizing their weakness, struck from the north; the Wuhuan entered from the east; Wusun struck from the west—the three states together killed tens of thousands, seized tens of thousands of horses, and very many cattle and sheep;

sentences.zh: 又重以餓死，人民死者什三，畜產什五。

translations.literal: and moreover, with starvation added, of the people three-tenths died and of livestock five-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: and with starvation added, three-tenths of the people and five-tenths of the livestock perished.

sentences.zh: 匈奴大虛弱，諸國羈屬者皆瓦解，攻盜不能理。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu were greatly weakened; all states bound in submission dissolved, and raids and theft could not be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu were greatly weakened; all subordinate states broke away, and raids and banditry could not be controlled.

sentences.zh: 其後漢出三千餘騎為三道，並入匈奴，捕虜得數千人還；

translations.literal: Afterward Han sent out more than three thousand horsemen in three columns, together entering the Xiongnu, capturing prisoners numbering several thousand and returning;
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Han sent out more than three thousand horsemen in three columns into Xiongnu territory, captured several thousand prisoners, and returned;

sentences.zh: 匈奴終不敢取當，滋欲鄉和親，而邊境少事矣。

translations.literal: the Xiongnu in the end did not dare meet them in battle, increasingly wished to turn toward peace by marriage, and border affairs grew few.
translations.idiomatic: the Xiongnu in the end did not dare meet them in battle, increasingly wished to seek peace through marriage, and border affairs grew quiet.

sentences.zh: ----8是歲，穎川太守趙廣漢為京兆尹。

translations.literal: ----8 That year, Governor of Yingchuan Zhao Guanghan became Metropolitan Magistrate of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: ----8 That year, Governor of Yingchuan Zhao Guanghan became metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 穎川俗，豪桀相朋黨。

translations.literal: Yingchuan custom: powerful men formed factions with one another.
translations.idiomatic: In Yingchuan custom, powerful men formed factions with one another.

sentences.zh: 廣漢為缿筒，受吏民投書，使相告訐，於是更相怨咎，奸黨散落，盜賊不敢發。

sentences.zh: 廣漢聰明，皆知其能之所宜，盡力與否；

translations.literal: Guanghan was perceptive and clear; he all knew what each man's ability suited and whether he exerted his strength or not;

sentences.zh: 其發奸擿伏如神。

translations.literal: His exposing wickedness and plucking out hidden matters was like a spirit's.
translations.idiomatic: His exposing crime and uncovering hidden plots was uncanny.

sentences.zh: 京兆政清，吏民稱之不容口。

translations.literal: Jingzhao's government was clear; clerks and people praised him without room left in the mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao's government was clear; clerks and people praised him without end.

sentences.zh: 長老傳以為自漢興，治京兆者莫能及。

translations.literal: The elders transmitted that since Han's rise, none who governed Jingzhao could match him.
translations.idiomatic: The elders transmitted that since Han's rise, none who governed Jingzhao could match him.

sentences.zh: 1春，三月，乙卯，立霍光女為皇后，赦天下。

translations.idiomatic: 1 In spring, the third month, on yimao, Huo Guang's daughter was established as empress and there was an amnesty for all under Heaven.

translations.idiomatic: The ancestral temples of Beihai and Langye were ruined.

translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the chancellor, censor, marquises, and two-thousand-bushel officials broadly to consult scholars of the classics for means to respond to the calamity, without concealment.

sentences.zh: 大赦天下。

translations.literal: There was a great amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: There was a great amnesty for all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 上素服，避正殿五日。

translations.literal: The emperor wore plain dress and avoided the main hall for five days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore plain dress and avoided the main hall for five days.

sentences.zh: 釋夏侯勝、黃霸，以勝為諫大夫、給事中，霸為揚州刺史。

translations.idiomatic: He released Xiahou Sheng and Huang Ba, making Sheng remonstrance grandee and attendant within the gates, and Ba governor of Yangzhou.

translations.idiomatic: Sheng was plain and upheld rectitude, simple and without imposing deportment; sometimes he called the emperor "lord" and mistakenly used familiar terms in his presence;

sentences.zh: 上亦以是親信之。

translations.literal: the emperor also on this account was close to and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor also for this reason was close to and trusted him.

translations.idiomatic: Once after an audience he repeated the emperor's words on the road; the emperor heard and reproached Sheng; Sheng said, "What Your Majesty said was good—your servant therefore spread it.

sentences.zh: 堯言佈於天下，至今見誦。

translations.literal: Yao's words were spread through all under Heaven and to this day are seen recited.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's words were spread through all under Heaven and are recited to this day.

sentences.zh: 臣以為可傳，故傳耳。

translations.literal: Your servant thought they could be transmitted, and therefore transmitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant thought they should be transmitted, and therefore transmitted them.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷每有大議，上知勝素直，謂曰：「先生建正言，無懲前事！

translations.literal: " Whenever the court had great deliberations, the emperor, knowing Sheng was by nature upright, said to him: "Master, set forth correct words—do not be chastened by former affairs!
translations.idiomatic: " Whenever the court had great deliberations, the emperor, knowing Sheng was by nature upright, said to him, "Master, set forth correct words—do not be chastened by former affairs!

sentences.zh: 」勝復為長信少府，後遷太子太傅。

translations.idiomatic: " Sheng was again made director of Changxin Household and later transferred to grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 年九十卒，太后賜錢二百萬，為勝素服五日，以報師傅之恩。

translations.literal: At age ninety he died; the empress dowager bestowed two million cash, wore plain dress for Sheng for five days, to repay the grace of a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: He died at age ninety; the empress dowager bestowed two million cash and wore plain dress for him for five days to repay a teacher's grace.

translations.idiomatic: Confucians took this as an honor.

translations.idiomatic: 1 In spring, Huo Guang's illness was grave.

translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally came to inquire; he wept for him.

translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengwu, Guang died.

translations.idiomatic: an edict was issued to restore his later generations, grant his noble fief in perpetuity, generation after generation without any levy.

translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wei Xiang submitted a sealed memorial: "The state has newly lost the grand general; it is fitting to display meritorious ministers to fill the feudal states, not leave great offices empty, to block contention for power.

translations.idiomatic: Since the Houyuan era, emoluments have departed from the royal house and government has lain with the chief steward.

sentences.zh: 今光死，子復為右將軍，兄子秉樞機，昆弟、諸婿據權勢，在兵官，光夫人顯及諸女皆通籍長信宮，或夜詔門出入，驕奢放縱，恐寢不制，宜有以損奪其權，破散陰謀，以固萬世之基，全功臣之世。

translations.literal: Now Guang is dead, his son again is Right General, his elder brother's son holds the pivot of power, brothers and sons-in-law hold authority in military offices, Guang's wife Xian and all daughters have registry at Changxin Palace, some enter and leave by night edict gates in arrogant extravagance and unbridled license—I fear they will not be controlled in sleep; there should be means to diminish and seize their power, break up secret plots, to secure the foundation of ten thousand generations and preserve the generations of meritorious ministers.

translations.literal: The pivot of power was close and thorough; grades and models were fully provided; above and below were at peace, and none had a perfunctory mind.
translations.idiomatic: The pivot of power was close and thorough; grades and models were fully provided; above and below were at peace, and none were perfunctory.

sentences.zh: 及拜刺史、守、相，輒親見問，觀其所由，退而考察所行以質其言，有名實不相應，必知其所必然。

translations.literal: When appointing governors, prefects, and chancellors of states, he immediately personally received them and questioned them, observing their origins; afterward he examined their conduct to verify their words—if name and reality did not correspond, he was sure to know what would necessarily follow.
translations.idiomatic: When appointing governors, prefects, and chancellors of states, he immediately personally received and questioned them, observing their origins; afterward he examined their conduct to verify their words—if name and reality did not correspond, he was sure to know what would follow.

sentences.zh: 常稱曰：「庶民所以安其-{田里}-而亡歎息愁恨之心者，政平訟理也。

translations.literal: He often said: "The reason the common people can settle their -{田里}- and be without sighing and resentful hearts is that government is level and lawsuits are settled.
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "The reason the common people can settle their -{田里}- and be without sighing and resentful hearts is that government is level and lawsuits are settled.

sentences.zh: 與我共此者，其唯良二千石乎！

translations.literal: Those who share this with me—are they not the good two-thousand-bushel officials!
translations.idiomatic: Those who share this with me—are they not the good two-thousand-bushel officials!

sentences.zh: 」以為太守，吏民之本，數變易則下不安；

translations.literal: " He held that the governor is the root of clerks and people; frequent changes make those below unsettled;
translations.idiomatic: " He held that the governor is the root of clerks and people; frequent changes make those below unsettled;

sentences.zh: 民知其將久，不可欺罔，乃服從其教化。

translations.literal: when the people know he will be long in office and cannot be deceived, then they submit to his transforming instruction.
translations.idiomatic: when the people know he will be long in office and cannot be deceived, then they submit to his transforming instruction.

sentences.zh: 故二千石有治理效，輒以璽書勉厲，增秩，賜金，或爵至關內侯；

translations.literal: Therefore when a two-thousand-bushel official had governing effect, he immediately sent a seal-letter to encourage and urge him, increased his rank, bestowed gold, or ennobled him to Marquis Within the Passes;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when a two-thousand-bushel official had governing effect, he immediately sent a seal-letter to encourage him, increased his rank, bestowed gold, or ennobled him to marquis within the passes;

sentences.zh: 公卿缺，則選諸所表，以次用之。

translations.literal: when a high minister's office was vacant, he selected from those recommended, using them in order.
translations.idiomatic: when a high minister's office was vacant, he selected from those recommended, using them in order.

sentences.zh: 是以漢世良吏，於是為盛，稱中興焉。

translations.literal: Thus in the Han age good officials were then at their flourishing, and it was called the Restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in the Han age good officials flourished as never before, and the era was called the Restoration.

sentences.zh: ----5匈奴壺衍鞮單于死，弟左賢王立為虛閭權渠單于，以右大將女為大閼氏，而黜前單于所幸顓渠閼氏。

translations.literal: ----5 Chanyu Huyandi of the Xiongnu died; his younger brother the Left Wise King was established as Chanyu Xulüquanqu, took the Right Grand General's daughter as great yanzhi, and dismissed the former chanyu's favored Zhuanqu yanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 Chanyu Huyandi of the Xiongnu died; his younger brother the Left Wise King became Chanyu Xulüquanqu, made the Right Grand General's daughter chief queen, and demoted the former chanyu's favored Zhuanqu.

sentences.zh: 顓渠閼氏父左大且渠怨望。

translations.literal: Zhuanqu yanzhi's father, the Left Grand Daqu, bore resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanqu's father, the Left Grand Daqu, nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 是時漢以匈奴不能為邊寇，罷塞外諸城以休百姓。

translations.literal: At this time Han, because the Xiongnu could not raid the borders, abolished the various cities beyond the passes to rest the common people.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Han, seeing the Xiongnu could not raid the borders, dismantled outpost cities beyond the passes to spare the people.

sentences.zh: 單于聞之，喜，召貴人謀，欲與漢和親。

translations.literal: The chanyu heard it and was pleased; he summoned nobles to deliberate and wished to make peace kinship with Han.
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu rejoiced, summoned his nobles to counsel, and wished to seek peace kinship with Han.

sentences.zh: 左大且渠心害其事，曰：「前漢使來，兵隨其後。

translations.literal: The Left Grand Daqu inwardly resented the affair and said: "Previously when Han envoys came, troops followed behind them.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Grand Daqu inwardly opposed the plan and said, "Previously when Han envoys came, troops followed behind them.

sentences.zh: 今亦效漢發兵，先使使者入。

translations.literal: Now too imitate Han in raising troops—first send envoys in.
translations.idiomatic: Now imitate Han: raise troops and send envoys in first.

sentences.zh: 」乃自請與呼盧訾王各將萬騎，南旁塞獵，相逢俱入。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he himself requested that he and King Hulüze each lead ten thousand horsemen south to hunt beside the barrier, meet, and enter together.
translations.idiomatic: " He then volunteered that he and King Hulüze each lead ten thousand horsemen south to hunt along the border, meet up, and enter together.

sentences.zh: 行未到，會三騎亡降漢，言匈奴欲為寇。

translations.literal: Before they had gone, it happened that three riders fled and surrendered to Han, saying the Xiongnu wished to raid.
translations.idiomatic: Before they arrived, three riders defected to Han and reported that the Xiongnu intended to raid.

sentences.zh: 於是天子詔發邊騎屯要害處，使大將軍軍監治眾等四人將五千騎，分三隊，出塞各數百里，捕得虜各數十人而還。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Son of Heaven ordered border cavalry to encamp at critical points and sent four army supervisors of the Grand General such as Zhi Zhong, each leading five thousand horsemen in three columns beyond the passes several hundred li each, capturing several tens of captives each and returning.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the emperor ordered border cavalry to garrison chokepoints and sent four Grand General's army supervisors including Zhi Zhong, each with five thousand horsemen in three columns beyond the passes for several hundred li each, capturing several tens of captives apiece before returning.

sentences.zh: 時匈奴亡其三騎，不敢入，即引去。

translations.literal: At that time the Xiongnu, having lost those three riders, did not dare enter and at once withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu, missing those three riders, did not dare enter and at once withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是歲，匈奴饑，人民、畜產死者什六七，又發兩屯各萬騎以備漢。

translations.literal: That year the Xiongnu suffered famine; of the people and livestock six or seven tenths died, and they also raised two encampments of ten thousand horsemen each to guard against Han.
translations.idiomatic: That year famine struck the Xiongnu; six or seven tenths of the people and livestock perished, and they still posted two camps of ten thousand horsemen each against Han.

sentences.zh: 其秋，匈奴前所得西嗕居左地者，其君長以下數千人皆驅畜產行，與甌脫戰，所殺傷甚眾，遂南降漢。

translations.literal: That autumn those the Xiongnu had earlier taken from the Western Ruo dwelling in the left zone—from chiefs downward, several thousand in all—all drove livestock on the march, fought Ouduo, killed and wounded very many, and thereupon went south to surrender to Han.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn several thousand western captives the Xiongnu had held in the left zone—from chiefs downward—drove their herds forth, fought their Ouduo guards, inflicted heavy casualties, and defected south to Han.
